items.title: Tinubu’s economic reforms key to sustainable security, says Dare
items.description: Former Minister of Youth and Sports Development, Sunday Dare, has said President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms and social interventions constitute an important part of a sustainable national security strategy, arguing that insecurity cannot be tackled through military operations alone. Dare, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Thursday, said economic development, effective governance and social inclusion were critical to addressing the underlying conditions that fuel insecurity. He observed that public discussions on national security often focused largely on military interventions, while overlooking the structural impact of economic policies and social programmes on the factors that sustain insecurity. According to him, states with poor developmental indices often record high levels of fragility, reinforcing the need to complement military operations with investments in development and effective governance. Dare cited the security intervention in Birnin Gwari, Kaduna State, as an example of how improved security could support economic recovery and restore livelihoods. He said the intervention by Tinubu had enabled farmers to return to their farms, created employment opportunities for young people and improved productivity. He also credited Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, with providing an account of the development and its impact on communities in the area. Highlighting some of the Federal Government’s policies with security implications, Dare identified the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), local government autonomy and increased Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) allocations to states and local governments. On NELFUND, he said expanding access to tertiary education would promote social inclusion and create opportunities for young people who might otherwise be excluded from educational advancement. According to him, providing legitimate pathways to education and economic opportunities could reduce the vulnerability of young people to recruitment by insurgents and other violent groups. He described education not merely as a social investment but also as a long-term investment in national security. On local government autonomy, Dare said adequately resourced and accountable councils could strengthen government presence in communities through improved public services and development initiatives. He argued that responsive governance at the grassroots would reduce the opportunities for violent non-state actors to exploit poorly governed communities and public disaffection. The former minister also said improved FAAC allocations could enhance the capacity of state and local governments to invest in infrastructure, education, healthcare, employment and other essential services. He, however, stressed that such resources must be transparently and productively deployed to address socioeconomic grievances and vulnerabilities that contribute to insecurity. Dare maintained that security should be assessed not only by the government’s ability to confront threats through military force but also by its capacity to address the conditions that make insecurity possible. He noted that military operations remained necessary, particularly in confronting active armed groups, but argued that their gains would be more sustainable when supported by inclusive development, strong institutions and responsive governance. He urged Nigerians to broaden the national conversation on security performance by giving greater consideration to the developmental and social impact of government policies. items.title: 2027 Budget: Ato Forson pledges disciplined use of fiscal space to create jobs and boost production
items.description: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says the government must use every cedi of fiscal space to generate jobs, strengthen domestic production and create lasting value for Ghanaians. Presenting the 2027 Budget to Parliament on Thursday, November 12, 2026, he said the government’s economic recovery had created an opportunity that must be directed towards productive investment. “Every cedi of that space must answer a national question: What jobs will it create? What import will it replace? What export will it generate? And what lasting value will it leave behind? Our economic programme, the New Economy, provides that answer,” he said. Dr Forson said the government had a moral obligation to use the fiscal space responsibly and ensure that the benefits of economic recovery translated into improved livelihoods. The Finance Minister said Ghana had previously created fiscal space but failed to channel it consistently into investments capable of transforming the economy. He noted that after immediate economic pressures eased, scarce resources were often spread across competing demands, while projects were initiated without rigorous appraisal. “Once the immediate pressures eased, scarce resources were spread thinly across competing demands. Projects multiplied without rigorous appraisal, and short-term consumption crowded out investment in productive capacity,” he said. “We repaired the public finances, but we did not use that recovery to alter the structure of our economy.” He said the government’s New Economy programme was intended to address that weakness by linking fiscal stability to production, employment and long-term economic value. Dr Forson also acknowledged the sacrifices households had endured during periods of economic instability. He said the value of the recovery would ultimately be measured by whether it improved people’s lives through employment, higher incomes and greater economic opportunities. “No statistic can refund the years families lost to instability. Their sacrifices will be earned when we restore stability—when stability becomes production, jobs, rising income, and opportunities,” he said. The Finance Minister said Ghana’s gross international reserves had increased to the equivalent of 5.7 months of import cover. He said the improvement provided households and businesses with greater certainty and gave the country room to plan beyond immediate economic pressures. “These gains give households greater certainty, allow businesses to plan, and create room for Ghanaians to think beyond the next emergency and crisis,” he said. Parliament is expected to begin debate on the 2027 Budget in the coming days, with the Appropriation Bill to follow.

items.title: Concerned Small-Scale Miners demand investigations into Manso Kaniago killings
items.description: The National Concerned Small-Scale Miners Association says the fight against illegal mining must not be waged at the expense of human lives and constitutional rights. This follows the clash between operatives of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and residents of Manso Keniago in the Ashanti Region, which has resulted in six deaths and left many injured. The group insists that the incident must be treated as a human rights concern. “The killing of citizens must not be treated as an ordinary operational incident. Where there are allegations of unlawful use of force resulting in death, the matter must be treated as a serious criminal and human rights concern,” the Association stated. In a press release signed by its President, Michael Kwadwo Peprah, the Association extended condolences to the bereaved families and the entire Manso Kaniago community, while strongly condemning what it described as the loss of innocent lives. They further demanded an immediate, independent and impartial investigation into the killings, with direct presidential intervention from President John Dramani Mahama. “The mere ownership or possession of an excavator is not, in itself, a criminal offence under Ghanaian law. Therefore, law enforcement operations must be guided by the law, proper procedures and respect for the fundamental rights of citizens,” it said. The Association stressed that it is not opposed to the operations of NAIMOS or the government’s efforts to combat illegal mining, but warned that the alleged actions of a few individuals could undermine the credibility of the entire anti-galamsey fight. It cautioned against a shoot-to-kill approach, noting that such acts are unsustainable. While calling for accountability for any officer found to have acted unlawfully and a review of NAIMOS operational procedures, the Association emphasised that environmental protection cannot be separated from human rights. “The fight against illegal mining must not become a fight against innocent citizens. Environmental protection and the enforcement of mining laws must go hand in hand with respect for human life, justice and the rule of law,” it added. The group appealed to President Mahama to act swiftly before the incident develops into a broader national concern and creates public resentment against the government, warning that failure to address incidents involving the alleged excessive use of state power can have serious political and public consequences. The Association reaffirmed its commitment to responsible mining and support for the fight against illegal mining, but said it will not remain silent when the lives and rights of citizens are allegedly put at risk in the name of enforcement, insisting that justice must be served and the people of Manso Kaniago deserve answers.

items.title: 2027: Opposition parties lack experience to govern Nigeria, says Ambode
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Former Lagos State Governor, Akinwunmi Ambode, has criticised opposition parties seeking to unseat the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections, saying they lack the political experience and leadership depth required to govern Nigeria. Ambode specifically mentioned the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and other opposition platforms, arguing that the APC had greater political experience and ideological consistency. He spoke at the APC East Senatorial District rally held at Epe Recreational Ground, Epe, Lagos State, where he canvassed support for President Bola Tinubu, the party’s Lagos governorship candidate, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, and other APC candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. Ambode said the APC had remained consistent in its political identity, unlike some politicians who, according to him, frequently moved from one political party to another. “APC is our party. We are a collective of the progressives. We have been consistent and delivering for the party. Over the years, we have remained with the progressives and we do not move from one party to another like other people,” he said. Describing the APC as a party connecting the country’s past, present and future, the former governor argued that its political experience placed it in a different position from opposition parties seeking to take over the reins of government. He also credited Tinubu’s political vision and record as Lagos governor with contributing to the state’s economic and infrastructural development, particularly its emergence as a major investment destination. Ambode said the foundations laid during Tinubu’s tenure as governor helped create an environment for financial institutions and corporate organisations to establish and expand their operations in Lagos. “Whether you like him or not, he is a visionary leader. If not for Tinubu, who laid the foundation for the Lagos of today, all the financial firms that have their headquarters in Lagos would have been struggling to survive. But today, his vision has assisted the country to remain an investor destination,” he said. He urged Lagos residents and Nigerians across different social and economic backgrounds to support the APC in the forthcoming elections. Ambode also appealed to members of the Igbo community living in Lagos and other parts of the country to consider national unity and their economic interests when making political choices. “To my Igbo brothers, wherever you live and get your prosperity, that is where you should call home. items.title: “I am hopeful we can have another good game on Monday” – Kim Lars Björkegren
items.description: The Black Stars returned to winning ways with a 2-0 victory over Somalia in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign at the Essipong Sports Stadium in Takoradi on Thursday. The result marked Ghana’s first win since their defeats to Côte d’Ivoire and The Gambia in the previous qualifying matches, offering some relief after a difficult start to the campaign. It was also a new beginning for the Black Stars following the dismissal of head coach Carlos Queiroz, with Kim Lars Björkegren taking charge as interim coach, assisted by Godwin Attram and Ibrahim Tanko. Ghana made a winning return to the Essipong Sports Stadium for the first time in 17 years, with defender Jonas Adjetey among the goalscorers as the hosts secured all three points. Despite the victory, Björkegren admitted his side were below their best in the opening half, pointing to the conditions in Takoradi as one of the factors behind their slow start. “We were struggling a little bit. I don’t know if the heat was too much, but the intensity was a bit low in the first half,” he said after the game. The interim coach, however, was pleased with the response after the break, believing Ghana showed greater energy and control as the game progressed. “We raised our energy, entertained the fans and had good chances. Overall, we controlled the game, even if we did not take all our chances. I am happy for the win and hopeful we can have another good game on Monday,” he added. Björkegren also acknowledged areas that need improvement ahead of the return fixture, particularly Ghana’s speed of play and efficiency in front of goal. “I think we can play the ball a bit faster than we did, especially in the first half. But I respect the effort because the heat makes it not easy to play. “Of course, we can improve on many aspects from today’s game, especially in terms of taking our chances.” For Adjetey, the victory was made more memorable by his first goal for the senior national team. The defender expressed his delight at finally getting on the scoresheet, crediting his teammates for their support. “It feels amazing to score my first goal. I have been waiting for this moment for some time now. My teammates have been very supportive and I am glad that I had such an opportunity,” he said. The Black Stars defender also welcomed the clean sheet, insisting the team had worked to correct the defensive mistakes that contributed to their previous defeats. “Unfortunately, we did our best in previous games but it did not go our way. The goals we conceded in the first two games had nothing to do with any individual or anything like that, but we have corrected our mistakes and it was good to keep a clean sheet today,” he added. The victory gives Björkegren a positive start to his interim tenure, although attention will quickly turn to Monday’s encounter as Ghana look to build on the result and maintain their momentum in Group C.

items.title: Pita : le corps sans vie d’un homme repêché dans la rivière Souma à Timbi-Madina
items.description: Le corps sans vie d’un homme de 36 ans, identifié comme Amadou Bah, a été découvert dans la rivière Souma, située entre les sous-préfectures de Timbi-Madina, dans la préfecture de Pita, et de Diari, dans la préfecture de Labé. Selon une source locale, la victime, qui souffrait de troubles mentaux depuis son enfance, était portée disparue depuis plusieurs jours avant cette découverte macabre. Joint au téléphone ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026, le maire de la commune rurale de Timbi-Madina, Mamadou Lamine Diallo, est revenu sur les circonstances de la découverte du corps. « Hier, aux environs de 16 heures, les responsables de la jeunesse du district de Tiapata nous ont informés que des jeunes avaient découvert un corps sans vie dans la rivière située entre les sous-préfectures de Diari et de Timbi-Madina. Nous avons aussitôt alerté le sous-préfet, les services de sécurité et les agents de santé, avant de nous rendre sur les lieux. Des jeunes volontaires et des gendarmes ont ensuite plongé dans l'eau pour repêcher le corps. D'après nos constatations, la noyade remontait à plusieurs jours », a-t-il expliqué. Le maire précise qu'au moment de la découverte, l'identité du défunt n'était pas connue. Toutefois, un petit seau et des chaussures avaient été retrouvés sur la rive, du côté de Diari. Le corps a finalement été inhumé aux environs de 19 heures, tandis que des photos prises par les services de sécurité ont été diffusées afin de permettre à ses proches de l'identifier. C'est par la suite que les autorités locales ont été informées de la disparition d'un jeune homme souffrant de troubles mentaux dans le district de Tiapata. Les clichés ont alors été présentés à sa famille, qui a formellement reconnu le défunt. La victime, Amadou Bah, était âgée de 36 ans, célibataire et sans enfant. Elle souffrait de troubles mentaux depuis son enfance, a conclu Mamadou Lamine Diallo. Alpha Moussa Dieng, correspondant régional à Labé L’article Pita : le corps sans vie d’un homme repêché dans la rivière Souma à Timbi-Madina est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: I won’t leave England before Euro 2028 —Tuchel
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Thomas Tuchel has ruled out leaving England for a club job before Euro 2028, saying he wants to see out his contract and complete what he calls “unfinished business” with the national team. According to ESPN, Tuchel said there was “no release clause” in his England contract and “no intention” of leaving before the tournament. His comments come amid Manchester United’s move to replace Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino. “I signed a contract; I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business,” Tuchel said. The German succeeded Gareth Southgate in 2025 and signed a two-year extension in February, keeping him in charge through Euro 2028. Tuchel said he was “open for everything” once his contract ends, including staying with England, but confirmed he eventually wants to return to club management. “Yes, definitely,” he said when asked if he would return to club football. “I miss the 50 matches. I miss these two minutes when everything is done.” Tuchel said he also understood the pressures of the club game, where matches come every few days. He said he was grateful for his England role and the freedom to work with his staff. “I’m very grateful for what I have here because I know how rare it is to be in love with your team and to have the trust and to be able to work freely with your coaching staff, which I am,” he said. Tuchel also said he felt aligned with the Football Association from their first discussions and valued the trust of chief executive Mark Bullingham and chief football officer Dan Ashworth. “That’s what you look for as a coach,” he said. “I love my group of players. I love my staff, and I have bosses who trust me and are happy with the way we do things, so it’s a lot. “I appreciate it a lot, so it’s in a good place, I’m in a good place, and I love the players. I miss my players, and I miss my team, and I miss the 50 matches that I’m not involved in a year. “But I’m desperate to win the Nations League and to play and try to win the Euros.” The post I won’t leave England before Euro 2028 —Tuchel appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Benue approves N5.2bn for NG-CARES, salary arrears
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Benue State Executive Council has approved a total of N5.2 billion for the implementation of the second phase of the Nigeria Community Action for Resilience and Economic Stimulus (NG-CARES 2.0) programme and the payment of 12 months’ outstanding salary arrears owed academic staff of tertiary institutions in the state. The approvals were among the major decisions reached at the State Executive Council meeting held at Government House, Makurdi. Briefing journalists after the meeting, the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Mr Solomon Iorpev, said N2.9 billion was approved for NG-CARES 2.0, while N2.3 billion was earmarked for the settlement of the salary arrears. He also announced the approval of 25 and 35 per cent salary increments for members of the Academic Staff Union of Tertiary Institutions of Benue State (ASUTIBS), with an additional monthly financial commitment of N191.9 million. Iorpev further disclosed that the council approved the domestication of the Consolidated Legislative Salary Structure (CONLESS) for staff of the State House of Assembly and the House of Assembly Commission. The council also approved N498.9 million as a variation for the ongoing rural electrification project covering 12 communities along the Ihugh axis of Vandeikya Local Government Area. The Commissioner for Rural Development and Cooperatives, Dr Ortese Yanmar, who disclosed this, said the project was about 90 per cent completed. He listed some of the beneficiary communities as Ihugh, Bako, Abaki, Tse-Alia, Mbausu, Ngehe, Hembe and Anhyula. According to him, the variation became necessary following an increase in the cost of materials, expressing optimism that the project would be completed before Christmas. On NG-CARES 2.0, the Commissioner for Finance, Mr Michael Oglegba, explained that the programme had previously supported rural communities through borehole projects, renovation of schools, provision of health facilities, cash transfers and business support. He said the fresh approval would sustain and expand the interventions across the state, particularly in communities and households requiring government assistance. Also speaking, the Director-General of the Benue State Budget and Economic Planning Commission, Prof. Jerome Andohol, disclosed that the council approved the domestication of the National Chart of Accounts and the adoption of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS)-compliant budgeting for local governments. He said the initiative would harmonise budgeting and financial reporting at the local government level, strengthen accountability and ensure the efficient utilisation of public resources. Andohol further revealed that the state’s social register currently contained close to 500,000 vulnerable households, representing approximately 1.7 million people, captured under the NG-CARES intervention framework. Meanwhile, the council celebrated Princess Adeja International College, Gboko, for emerging as the overall best international secondary school in the country for the sixth consecutive time at the Nigerian International Secondary School Model United Nations Competition. The school also clinched 37 individual awards at the competition. The Commissioner for Education and Knowledge Management, Dr Margaret Adamu, disclosed that Government Girls’ College, Makurdi, which represented the state at a competition organised by the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies, finished third at the North-Central level. On security, Iorpev said the council received encouraging reports of relative calm across the state, assuring that Benue remained open to visitors and political campaigners who complied with due process and necessary security protocols. He, however, emphasised that individuals seeking access to internally displaced persons’ camps managed by the state government must obtain the necessary permission and clearance before embarking on such visits. items.title: Burkinabè contraints de quitter la Guinée: les acteurs nationaux et régionaux mobilisés autour des défis
items.description: (Ouagadougou, le 12 novembre 2026) Face à la situation des compatriotes contraints de quitter la Guinée, la Présidente du Conseil national de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CONASUR), le Camarade Ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité le Lieutenant-colonel Passowendé Pélagie KABORE, a convoqué une réunion de coordination avec les membres sectoriels du Conseil et les gouverneurs des dix-sept régions du Burkina Faso. Cette rencontre avait pour objectif de partager une situation actualisée de l'opération, de mettre l'ensemble des acteurs au même niveau d'information et d'examiner les dispositions nécessaires à sa poursuite dans les meilleures conditions. Composé de plusieurs départements et structures sectoriels au niveau national, le CONASUR s'appuie, au niveau régional, sur les Conseils régionaux de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CORESUR), placés sous la coordination des gouverneurs. Cette organisation constitue un levier essentiel pour assurer la cohérence des interventions, faciliter la remontée des informations et adapter les réponses aux réalités du terrain. La ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité, le Lieutenant-colonel Passowendé Pélagie Kaboré La réunion a permis de faire le point des actions déjà engagées par le Gouvernement. Depuis le déclenchement du dispositif interministériel de gestion de crise par le Premier ministre, le 3 novembre 2026, plusieurs mesures ont été mises en œuvre pour faciliter le retour des compatriotes et organiser leur prise en charge. Sur le plan logistique, 156 cars et 44 camions ont été mobilisés, avec l’organisation de cinq convois entre les zones de regroupement au Mali et le Burkina Faso. Au cours des échanges, les membres du CONASUR ont également été informés de l'ampleur de la situation. A la date de la réunion, plus de 43 800 compatriotes avaient regagné le territoire national. Ce chiffre témoigne de l'importance de la mobilisation engagée et de l'ampleur des responsabilités qui incombent désormais aux structures nationales et territoriales. Les discussions ont permis de mettre en évidence les principaux défis auxquels le dispositif doit apporter des réponses. Les préoccupations sanitaires et sécuritaires demeurent particulièrement importantes. Elles exigent une vigilance constante dans les lieux d'accueil et de transit, ainsi qu'une coordination étroite entre les services compétents. L'identification des personnes dépourvues de documents d'identité et le rétablissement des liens familiaux figurent également parmi les préoccupations à prendre en compte. L'accompagnement des jeunes majeurs, notamment leur retour dans les localités d'origine et leur réinsertion socio-professionnelle, constitue un enjeu majeur de cette opération. L'affinement du profilage doit permettre de mieux cerner les situations individuelles et de proposer des réponses adaptées aux besoins de chacun. Une attention particulière devra être accordée aux enfants en âge scolaire ainsi qu'à la prévention de nouveaux départs vers les sites d'orpaillage, dans des conditions précaires. À l'issue des échanges, le Camarade Ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité a donné plusieurs orientations aux acteurs nationaux et régionaux afin de renforcer l'efficacité de l'intervention. Elle a notamment instruit les gouverneurs de prendre les dispositions nécessaires pour assurer un accueil digne et sécurisé des compatriotes dans les localités concernées, tout en veillant à ce que ces derniers puissent exprimer leurs préoccupations dans un cadre approprié. Elle a également insisté sur la nécessité d'organiser des séances de sensibilisation à l'intention des personnes rapatriées, particulièrement des jeunes, afin de déconstruire les perceptions qui entourent l'orpaillage et de leur faire connaître les possibilités de réinsertion socio-professionnelle. Cette démarche vise à leur présenter des perspectives alternatives et à prévenir leur retour vers des activités d'orpaillage exercées dans des conditions de précarité et d'insécurité. La poursuite de la mobilisation des ressources et des appuis disponibles au niveau local a également été recommandée pour soutenir les différentes étapes de l'opération. Les acteurs sont invités à renforcer la concertation et à inscrire leurs interventions dans une dynamique de complémentarité. La collecte et la diffusion des données devront s'effectuer en relation avec les autorités centrales ou déconcentrées compétentes, afin de garantir la fiabilité des informations et d'éviter les initiatives isolées. La Présidente du CONASUR a, par ailleurs, appelé au maintien d'un dialogue permanent entre les différentes parties prenantes. Le partage régulier des informations, la coordination des interventions et la communication sur les mesures engagées par les pouvoirs publics doivent permettre de rassurer les populations et de préserver la cohérence de l'action collective jusqu'à l'achèvement de l'opération. Après le retour de nos compatriotes sur le territoire national, l’enjeu est désormais de garantir leur accompagnement et leur réintégration dans des conditions dignes et adaptées à leurs situations . La mobilisation des structures sectorielles, des gouverneurs et des CORESUR sera déterminante pour assurer la continuité de cette prise en charge et faire du retour au pays une véritable perspective de reconstruction et de réinsertion. items.title: NAIMOS confirms discharge of two personnel injured in Manso Keniago clash
items.description: Two personnel of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS), who sustained gunshot wounds during a confrontation at Manso Keniago in the Ashanti Region, have been treated and discharged from hospital. The incident occurred on November 11, while a NAIMOS task force was transporting excavators seized during an anti-illegal mining operation to a designated location for safekeeping. Confirming their recovery, NAIMOS spokesperson, Paa Kwesi Schandorf, said both officers had received medical attention and were in stable condition. “The two NAIMOS personnel who were injured in yesterday’s clash have been treated and discharged. Their conditions remain stable,” he said. The discharge of the two officers comes amid reports that the confrontation claimed six lives and left several others injured. The clash reportedly stemmed from disagreements over the transportation of the seized excavators, with some residents and traditional authorities objecting to the decision to move the equipment through the community along a tarred road. The situation reportedly escalated when an armed group resisted the movement of the machinery, prompting NAIMOS personnel to fire warning shots, which the Secretariat said were intended to disperse the mob and prevent further escalation. However, the confrontation resulted in the deaths of three people and gunshot injuries to two NAIMOS personnel, while residents have accused the task force of initiating the violence. READ ALSO: Tensions rise in Manso Keniago as angry youth confront chief, accuse DCE over six deaths In its account of the incident, the Secretariat said its task force encountered an armed mob that attempted to obstruct the movement of the seized equipment. The officers reportedly fired warning shots to deter the group and prevent further escalation, but two personnel sustained gunshot wounds. Meanwhile, NAIMOS, in a statement issued on November 11, condemned the attack and cautioned individuals and groups against obstructing its personnel in the discharge of their duties. It described attacks, threats and other forms of violent resistance against its operations as unacceptable, insisting that such actions would not be tolerated. The Secretariat also reaffirmed its commitment to combating illegal mining, stressing that it would continue undertaking enforcement operations across the country despite acts of intimidation and resistance.

items.title: Sanwo-Olu, Ambode rally Lagos voters for Tinubu, Hamzat
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Governor, Mr Babajide Sanwo-Olu, and his predecessor, Mr Akinwunmi Ambode, have urged Lagos residents to support the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and the emergence of Deputy Governor, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, in the 2027 general elections. The duo made the call while addressing party faithful at the Lagos State All Progressives Congress (APC) East Senatorial District rally held at the Epe Recreational Ground, Epe. They applauded Tinubu’s contributions to Lagos State’s development, saying his administration as governor laid the foundation for the state’s sustained growth through deliberate policies, strategic planning and long-term infrastructure development. Sanwo-Olu urged residents to appreciate the President’s contributions by supporting his re-election for a second term. According to him, Tinubu deserves not only their votes but also their prayers and support, given his role in shaping Lagos into one of Africa’s most sought-after cities. “The President deserves more than our votes. He deserves our prayers and our support. I therefore urge Lagos residents to demonstrate their appreciation for the President’s leadership by turning out in large numbers on January 16 to express their support and vote massively for him,” he said. The governor noted that Tinubu’s transition from Lagos to the national stage had created an opportunity to extend his development philosophy across the country, with ongoing interventions and projects spanning the six geopolitical zones. He also acknowledged the Federal Government’s support for critical infrastructure projects in Lagos, including the proposed Green Line Rail and Lekki International Airport, saying the projects would improve connectivity, boost economic activities and strengthen the state’s position as a leading investment destination. Similarly, the Deputy Governor, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, said the rally was organised to canvass support for all APC candidates, urging residents to turn out en masse on election day. Hamzat said the Tinubu administration had recorded achievements in infrastructure, education, healthcare and other critical sectors, stressing the need for continuity. “On election day, let us not stay at home. Come out with your PVC and ensure that everyone in your neighbourhood votes. We have the highest number of registered voters in Nigeria. “Let us come out to vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and every candidate that will support the continuity of his good work,” he said. The senator representing Lagos East Senatorial District, Tokunbo Abiru, also urged residents to support Tinubu’s re-election, saying Lagos had capable leaders to sustain the administration’s development agenda. “We have capable people in Lagos. So, on election day, let us come out in our numbers to vote for all our candidates and ensure that they all return to power,” Abiru said. In his remarks, Ambode highlighted the APC’s longstanding presence in Lagos politics, noting that the party had maintained its political identity rather than moving between different platforms. He described the APC as a party that represented the people and emphasised the need for mutual cooperation between the party and the electorate. Using the expression, “the left hand washes the right hand, and the right hand washes the left hand,” Ambode urged party members and residents to support one another. He also contrasted the APC’s political history and governance experience with those of other political parties, which he described as relatively new. The Lagos State APC Chairman, Pastor Cornelius Ojelabi, urged eligible voters who were yet to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) to do so, describing the cards as essential instruments for participating in the democratic process. Ojelabi called on residents to exercise their civic responsibility, expressing confidence in the party’s development vision and stressing that unity remained its strength. Earlier, the Director-General of the PBAT-KOH Campaign Council in Lagos State, Senator Musiliu Obanikoro, urged residents to remain steadfast in their support for the APC and vote for all its candidates in the 2027 general elections. He said such support was necessary to sustain Lagos State’s tradition of progressive governance, continuity and development. Describing Tinubu and Hamzat as the most prepared leaders for the development of the country and Lagos State, respectively, Obanikoro said their experience and track records placed them in a strong position to advance the party’s development agenda. Also speaking, the Chairman of Ibeju-Lekki Local Government and Chairman of Conference 57, the umbrella body of the 57 local government areas and Local Council Development Areas in Lagos State, Mr Sesan Olowa, urged party members and supporters to intensify grassroots mobilisation across Lagos East. He called on them to take the APC’s message to households, neighbourhoods, communities, villages and towns across the senatorial district. items.title: ELIE SAAB Casablanca Art of Living inaugure son nouveau showroom et franchit un nouveau cap dans la commercialisation du projet
items.description: ART OF LIVING x EKTAR inaugurent le nouveau showroom d’ELIE SAAB Casablanca Art of Living, sur la route d’Azemmour. Une adresse incontournable pour découvrir, toucher et vivre en avant-première le premier projet résidentiel lifestyle brandé du Royaume. Conçu comme une immersion dans l'univers de la Maison ELIE SAAB, le showroom invite les visiteurs à découvrir l'identité architecturale, les matériaux et les finitions qui caractérisent cette collection exclusive de résidences. Il offre une première expérience concrète de l'art de vivre imaginé pour le domaine, avant sa livraison prévue fin 2028. Le showroom, vitrine de l’univers ELIE SAAB Bien plus qu’un espace de vente, le showroom a été pensé comme une véritable vitrine de l’univers ELIE SAAB, où les codes de la Haute Couture rencontrent ceux de l’architecture et du design d’intérieur. Jeux de matières, palettes de couleurs, lignes contemporaines et finitions raffinées composent un parcours immersif, conçu pour se projeter dans sa future résidence. Les visiteurs y découvrent les villas, appartements, duplex et penthouses du domaine, ainsi que les deux collections d’ambiances intérieures, Printemps/Été et Automne/Hiver, directement inspirées des collections Haute Couture de la Maison. Une adhésion qui se confirme L’inauguration intervient dans une dynamique commerciale soutenue. Moins d’un an après son lancement, le projet enregistre une commercialisation remarquable, portée notamment par ses villas et ses penthouses. Une clientèle exigeante, au Maroc comme à l’international, y a trouvé une promesse rare : une signature mondiale, une architecture d’exception et un art de vivre pensé dans ses moindres détails. « L’ouverture de ce showroom marque une étape importante dans la concrétisation de notre vision. L’accueil réservé au projet depuis son lancement confirme l’attente pour une offre qui associe une signature internationale, une architecture exigeante et une expérience de vie unique. Ce lieu donne aujourd’hui une dimension tangible à cette ambition », explique Salma Essoudi Bensouda, Head of ART OF LIVING. Quand la haute couture devient architecture Le domaine transpose dans la pierre les codes qui ont fait la renommée d’ELIE SAAB : des lignes pures, une lumière travaillée comme une étoffe, des matières nobles et ce sens du détail qui fait la différence. L’architecture porte la signature du studio international SAOTA, référence mondiale des résidences d’exception, associé à l’agence casablancaise GCAA – Ghali Chaoui Architecture et Associés. Les villas se distinguent par leurs lignes contemporaines, leurs volumes généreux et leur ouverture sur l’extérieur. Les appartements, duplex et penthouses, conçus dans un esprit de fluidité et d’élégance offrent des configurations de 2 à 4 chambres. Certaines résidences regardent l’océan. Toutes portent les intérieurs signés ELIE SAAB Maison. Vivre comme à l’hôtel, chez soi Ici, le luxe ne s’arrête pas à la porte d’entrée. Pensé selon les codes du branded serviced living, le domaine réunit l’intimité d’une résidence privée et les attentions d’un grand hôtel. Au coeur du domaine, un clubhouse privé de 1 000 m². Plonger dans la piscine chauffée au petit matin. Enchaîner une séance de fitness ou de yoga et un rendez-vous au Business Lounge. Travailler depuis l’espace de coworking, puis s’évader dans les jardins paysagers et sur les parcours de running et de promenade. Les enfants ont leurs espaces de jeux. Et pour tout le reste, une conciergerie dédiée veille au quotidien des résidents. Le temps retrouvé : voilà, peut-être, le plus grand des luxes. Un domaine qui sort de terre Le gros oeuvre, confié à GIDNA, l’un des acteurs de référence de la construction au Maroc, avance à bon rythme, pour une livraison prévue fin 2028. Le domaine s’engage aussi dans une certification HQE visant le niveau Excellent : un luxe conscient, pensé pour durer. Rendez-vous au showroom pour en vivre l’expérience, dès aujourd’hui. The post ELIE SAAB Casablanca Art of Living inaugure son nouveau showroom et franchit un nouveau cap dans la commercialisation du projet appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: La CAF ouvre les candidatures pour l'organisation des éditions 2028, 2031 et 2033 de la CAN
items.description: La Confédération africaine de football (CAF) a officiellement ouvert l'appel à candidatures pour l'organisation des trois prochaines éditions de la Coupe d'Afrique des Nations, prévues respectivement en 2028, 2031 et 2033. Cette démarche invite l'ensemble des fédérations nationales désireuses d'accueillir la grand-messe du football continental à manifester leur intérêt. Le calendrier fixé par l'instance faîtière du football africain s'annonce particulièrement serré : la date limite pour notifier son intention de se porter candidat a été arrêtée au 17 novembre en cours, tandis que le dépôt des dossiers complets devra intervenir au plus tard le 8 décembre prochain. La CAF a par ailleurs précisé que les associations membres ayant déjà exprimé leur intérêt pour l'une de ces échéances sont dispensées de renouveler leur déclaration formelle. Le cahier des charges offre par ailleurs de la souplesse aux pays postulants, autorisant le dépôt de candidatures conjointes impliquant deux États ou plus, de même qu'il est permis de briguer l'organisation de plusieurs éditions à la fois. Cette ouverture intervient dans le sillage de la révision du format de la compétition, l'instance dirigeante étant revenue sur son projet initial d'espacer le tournoi tous les quatre ans pour réinstaurer une périodicité biennale, tout en marquant une exception pour l'année 2030 en raison de la tenue de la Coupe du monde. items.title: Mahama assures Ghanaians old cedi notes remain valid alongside new Heritage Series
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has assured Ghanaians that the existing cedi banknotes will remain in circulation alongside the newly launched Heritage Series until commercial banks gradually withdraw the older notes. The clarification is intended to reassure traders, businesses and members of the public that transactions can continue using the existing currency as the new series enters circulation. Speaking at the launch of the Heritage Series at the Bank Square in Accra on Thursday, November 12, 2026, he said the introduction of the redesigned currency would be a gradual process, with both series serving as legal tender during the transition. “The new notes will run side by side with the old currency notes. They are not displacing the old currency notes. The banks will withdraw the old notes gradually until the new notes take over completely,” he said. President Mahama also reflected on the cedi’s resilience through Ghana’s economic challenges, noting that the currency had endured difficult periods and economic uncertainties that affected businesses and households. He described the cedi as an enduring symbol of Ghana’s economic sovereignty, despite the pressures it had faced over the years. He said the launch of the Heritage Series provided an opportunity to recognise not only the currency’s historical significance but also the patience, resilience and hard work of Ghanaians whose livelihoods depend on its strength. According to him, the next priority was to strengthen the economic foundations of the cedi through his government’s New Economy Programme. He said the programme was central to the 2027 national budget, which the Finance Minister was scheduled to present to Parliament later that day. The Heritage Series will be phased in gradually, allowing the existing and newly introduced banknotes to circulate concurrently until the transition is complete.

items.title: LGV Kénitra–Marrakech : Colas Rail décroche 29 M€ de travaux
items.description: Déjà engagé sur le chantier de la future ligne à grande vitesse, le groupe français Colas Rail s’adjuge un nouveau marché auprès de l’ONCF, centré sur le secteur de Casablanca. Le groupe Colas a annoncé ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026 que sa filiale Colas Rail avait remporté auprès de l’Office national des chemins de fer (ONCF) un nouveau contrat d’environ 29 millions d’euros. Ce marché s’inscrit dans le projet d’extension de la ligne à grande vitesse entre Kénitra et Marrakech. Il concerne un tronçon précis de la région casablancaise, situé entre la gare de Roches-Noires et le Technicentre de Nouaceur, le site dédié à la maintenance des trains. Le groupe, filiale de Bouygues, précise que ce montant correspond à une inscription au carnet de commandes en octobre 2026. D’après un communiqué du groupe, les travaux relèvent de trois domaines : la voie ferrée, le génie civil et la caténaire. Les prestations couvriront le réaménagement de voies existantes et la création de nouvelles, l’installation des équipements de caténaire, c’est-à-dire le dispositif d’alimentation électrique aérienne des trains, ainsi que les ouvrages de génie civil qui leur sont associés. Pour Hervé Le Joliff, Président de Colas Rail, ce contrat renforce un lien déjà ancien avec l’ONCF. « Le Maroc est un marché stratégique pour Colas Rail. Ce nouveau contrat avec l’ONCF s’inscrit dans une relation de long terme et confirme notre engagement aux côtés du développement de la grande vitesse dans le Royaume » , a-t-il déclaré. Colas Rail met en avant son ancrage local. L’entreprise est présente dans le Royaume depuis plus de 17 ans et s’appuie aujourd’hui sur environ 550 collaborateurs couvrant douze métiers complémentaires. Ses équipes ont réalisé plus de 40 chantiers à travers le pays et participé à plusieurs grandes opérations de modernisation du réseau ferroviaire marocain, notamment celles liées à la ligne à grande vitesse. Ce nouveau marché vient s’ajouter à deux contrats remportés en janvier 2025 sur le même projet, pour un montant total de 250 millions d’euros. Lors de leur annonce, le 5 février 2025, le groupe avait détaillé leur contenu, repris par la presse marocaine. Le premier, de 200 millions d’euros, porte sur la conception et la construction des voies, des caténaires et des sous-stations du lot nord. Le second, d’un montant de 50 millions d’euros, concerne des travaux de superstructure et de génie civil sur des voies déjà en exploitation. À l’époque, Colas avait aussi annoncé un troisième contrat, confié à sa filiale marocaine Les Grands Travaux Routiers (GTR) : le lot n° 3 des travaux de génie civil, estimé à près de 180 millions d’euros. L’ensemble représentait près de 430 millions d’euros de commandes. Le groupe avait inscrit ces chantiers dans la continuité de la ligne à grande vitesse reliant Tanger à Kénitra. Il présentait l’extension jusqu’à Marrakech comme une étape préparant l’accueil de la Coupe du monde 2030. Colas Rail connaît bien cette première ligne : elle y avait réalisé, entre 2014 et 2018, les travaux de voie et de caténaire. items.title: SIMANDOU 2040: la synchronisation logistique de MSC Guinée pour l’avenir économique du pays
items.description: Au cœur du Simandou Mining Summit, l’enjeu qui dépasse la simple extraction des ressources, est d'arrimer durablement la Guinée aux grands flux du commerce mondial. Depuis son stand, son Directeur Général en Guinée, Mael Atayi, détaille au micro de Guineenews l'engagement stratégique du leader mondial du transport maritime face aux exigences hors normes du mégaprojet Simandou. Une montée en puissance que MSC a su anticiper dès les phases initiales, en s'appuyant sur son statut. «, Aujourd'hui à MSC, on est le premier armateur mondial et donc on connecte le reste du monde à la Guinée. On est les leaders du marché en Guinée et pour ces raisons, on est un acteur privilégié du secteur minier et on accompagne nos clients sur l'ensemble de la chaîne logistique », affirme d’emblée Maël Atayi. Sur le terrain, cet engagement se traduit par des opérations menées sans relâche depuis plus de quatre ans pour acheminer les équipements lourds indispensables aux chantiers. « Aujourd'hui, le transport maritime n'est plus un point bloquant. Depuis 2022, nous avons acheminé des milliers de conteneurs pour le projet Simandou. Nous avons même acheminé des marchandises au gabarit hors paire et même des moteurs de plus de 100 tonnes pour faire de ce projet une réussite », précise-t-il. De la mer à la mine, la réponse «Project Cargo » Si la traversée des océans est parfaitement maîtrisée, le véritable défi opérationnel réside désormais dans la fluidité de bout en bout, depuis les quais portuaires jusqu'aux sites miniers les plus reculés. Et pour lever chaque goulot d'étranglement, MSC a déployé une ingénierie logistique dédiée. Selon son Directeur Général, «le vrai défi, c'est la synchronisation de toutes les étapes sur l'ensemble de la chaîne logistique. Pour y répondre, nous avons créé un département Project Cargo afin d'offrir des solutions sur mesure pour faire des projets miniers non plus des projets, mais une réalisation concrète en Guinée. » Un effet de levier pour l'économie guinéenne à l'horizon 2040 Autre point abordé dans cet entretien par Mael Atayi, c’est le rôle de locomotive que joue la dynamique minière pour l'ensemble du tissu économique national. « Quand le secteur minier est en croissance, c'est en réalité l'ensemble du pays qui est en croissance. Et aujourd'hui, la Guinée a le taux de croissance le plus dynamique de toute la sous-région et avec le programme Simandou 2040, ce n'est pas seulement le secteur minier qui est touché, c'est l'ensemble de l'économie guinéenne», analyse le dirigeant de MSC. Avant d’expliquer comment son groupe met l'intégralité de son réseau global au service des échanges du pays, pour soutenir cette ambition nationale. « … MSC, nous sommes présents dans 155 pays et nous avons une flotte de plus de 1 000 navires», insiste-t-il. Et de rassurer ensuite, «donc quand un conteneur arrive en Guinée ou part de la Guinée, c'est en réalité la force de tout ce réseau du groupe MSC qui se met au service de la Guinée pour répondre présent.» Dans la même logique, au-delà des multinationales minières, l'opérateur réaffirme sa volonté d'accompagner l'émergence du secteur privé national. « On voit qu'il y a énormément de projets et des entreprises locales qui veulent s'implanter en Guinée et on est vraiment heureux de pouvoir les accompagner et se mettre au service de cette croissance économique du pays », conclut Maël Atayi. Signant ainsi un engagement résolument tourné vers l'inclusion économique.

items.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO – The Sokoto State Government has approved ₦6.12 billion for the construction of nine Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) prototype schools across the state’s three senatorial districts. The government also approved additional funds for the rehabilitation and construction of mosques and the development of Islamic educational institutions across the state. The approvals were among the major decisions reached at Wednesday’s State Executive Council meeting, presided over by Governor Ahmed Aliyu at the Government House, Sokoto. Briefing journalists after the meeting, the Commissioner for Budget and Economic Planning, Dr Bashir Achida, said the nine UBEC prototype schools would be distributed equally among the three senatorial districts, with three schools allocated to each district. He said the initiative was aimed at expanding access to quality basic education, improving the learning environment and providing modern facilities for pupils, particularly in communities requiring better school infrastructure. Achida said the investment was in line with Governor Aliyu’s commitment to transforming the education sector under his administration’s Nine-Point SMART Agenda. On religious infrastructure, the council approved ₦221,548,705.25 for the rehabilitation of Achida Central Juma’at Mosque and ₦154,941,290 for the rehabilitation of Sabon Birni Central Juma’at Mosque. It also approved ₦98,242,007.50 for the construction of five daily prayer mosques in the Kwamberu area and ₦285,125,650.92 for the rehabilitation of Tureta Central Juma’at Mosque in Tureta Local Government Area. Similarly, ₦230,660,473.19 was approved for the rehabilitation of Kuppa Juma’at Mosque in the Gidan Sauro area. In the area of Islamic education, the council approved ₦166,982,489 for the construction of classrooms and sanitation facilities at Raddul Azzam Quranic School in Achida. Another ₦297,655,995.50 was approved for the construction of an Islamic school in Sabon Garin Tudun Wada area of Sokoto South Local Government Area. The commissioner further disclosed that ₦53,937,500 was approved for the provision of carpets at Gada Central Juma’at Mosque to improve facilities for congregational prayers. Achida said the approvals reflected the administration’s commitment to interventions in critical sectors, particularly basic education, religious development and community infrastructure. The projects, when completed, are expected to expand access to educational facilities, improve existing religious institutions and provide additional infrastructure for learning and worship across the state’s three senatorial districts. The post Sokoto approves ₦6.12bn for nine UBEC model schools appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NHIA welcomes GHS, CHAG directives against unauthorised NHIS charges
items.description: The National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) has welcomed directives issued by the Ghana Health Service (GHS) and the Christian Health Association of Ghana (CHAG) ordering their respective healthcare facilities to comply strictly with National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) requirements and stop imposing unauthorised charges on members. The directives, issued on November 9 and November 11, 2026, respectively, require healthcare providers to honour their obligations under the Scheme and ensure that patients are not compelled to make additional payments for services covered by the NHIS. The NHIA said the measures reinforce President John Dramani Mahama’s directive at the 68th Annual General Conference of the Ghana Medical Association, where he instructed the Authority to intensify monitoring of healthcare facilities, undertake facility-to-facility inspections and sanction institutions found charging NHIS members unauthorised fees. In a statement issued on Thursday, November 12, the Authority described the directives as an important demonstration of institutional commitment and collaboration towards protecting the rights of members and restoring public confidence in the Scheme. It said the development also reinforces the zero-tolerance campaign against illegal co-payments and unauthorised out-of-pocket charges being pursued by its Chief Executive, Dr Victor Asare Bampoe, since assuming office. The NHIA particularly welcomed CHAG’s directive to its member institutions to implement revised NHIA-approved tariffs, update their billing systems and strengthen internal compliance monitoring. It said the GHS directive similarly reaffirms the responsibility of healthcare facilities to fulfil their obligations under the NHIS. The Authority noted that the renewed enforcement measures come amid significant government interventions to improve the financial sustainability of the Scheme. These include the uncapping of the National Health Insurance Fund, regular monthly reimbursement of vetted claims and an approximately 50 per cent upward adjustment in NHIS service tariffs, which took effect in August 2026. As part of efforts to ensure timely payments to healthcare providers, the NHIA said it disbursed GH¢210.36 million to credentialed healthcare facilities in October alone. This brings the total amount paid in claims to healthcare providers in 2026 to GH¢2.325 billion. The Authority said it would intensify monitoring, investigations and enforcement activities to ensure that the directives issued by GHS and CHAG result in actual compliance at the facility level. It also pledged to strengthen collaboration with healthcare provider leadership, regional and district health directorates and other relevant stakeholders to monitor billing practices and investigate complaints of unauthorised charges. According to the NHIA, illegal co-payments and additional out-of-pocket charges place an unfair financial burden on vulnerable citizens and undermine public confidence in the Scheme. It said the directives from the two healthcare provider networks would add momentum to its nationwide compliance audits and taskforce operations aimed at eliminating the practice. The Authority thanked the Director-General of the GHS, Dr Samuel Kaba Akoriyea, and the Executive Director of CHAG, Dr Peter Yeboah, as well as other healthcare provider networks, for prioritising patient welfare. It reiterated its commitment to working with sector stakeholders to eliminate unauthorised fees and safeguard the integrity of the NHIS as Ghana advances towards Universal Health Coverage (UHC). The NHIA also reminded members that they are entitled to receive all services covered under the NHIS Benefit Package without being compelled to make unauthorised additional payments. Members who encounter facilities demanding extra payments for services covered by the Scheme have been encouraged to report such incidents to the Authority. Complaints can be lodged through the NHIA Call Centre on 6447 , 054 444 6447 or 0302 74 6447 . Members may also contact the Authority via WhatsApp on 0501 169 8778 or through its social media platforms. The NHIA stressed that the success of the Scheme depends not only on sustainable financing and timely reimbursement of healthcare providers but also on ensuring that members can access their entitled healthcare services without unauthorised financial barriers. It said it would continue working with the GHS, CHAG and all healthcare provider associations to protect members’ rights and ensure that the NHIS fulfils its mandate of shielding Ghanaians from the financial burden of accessing healthcare.

items.title: Menaces contre l’Algérie : El Djeich met en garde contre le triptyque désinformation-sabotage-drogues
items.description: Dans l’éditorial de son numéro de novembre 2026, la revue de l’Armée nationale populaire (ANP), El Djeich, est revenue sur les “tentatives auxquelles l’Algérie est confrontée et qui visent à porter atteinte à sa sécurité, à sa stabilité et à son unité”. Ces actions ont aussi pour but d’infléchir les “positions immuables” du pays, “sa trajectoire nationale et ses acquis”. Les trois formes que prennent les tentatives de nuire à l’Algérie Parmi les formes que prennent ces tentatives de nuire à l’Algérie, la revue de l’Armée nationale populaire cite “les campagnes de désinformation, de propagande et de manipulation”, les “odieuses campagnes de sabotage”, ainsi que le recours au crime organisé, notamment le trafic de drogue . L’objectif de leurs auteurs est de “semer le trouble et d’instiller le doute sur les grandes réalisations accomplies par notre pays ces dernières années”, lit-on dans l’éditorial. Mais ces plans et les complots ourdis contre l’Algérie “en pariant sur l’affaiblissement de la détermination de ses enfants et la division de leurs rangs”, ont “lamentablement échoué” et leurs instigateurs n’ont pas réussi à atteindre “leurs vils desseins et demeureront impuissantes face à un peuple uni, attaché à sa Patrie et à ses constantes”, se félicite la revue El Djeich. L’Algérie fière de son appartenance africaine Cette volonté se traduit par “la poursuite du processus d’édification et de développement, la consolidation de la position de l’Algérie en tant que pays fort et prospère, fidèle à ses positions immuables à l’égard des justes causes dans le monde, fier de son appartenance africaine et avançant avec assurance vers un avenir empreint de sécurité et de stabilité”, poursuit l'auteur de l’éditorial qui met en avant “les efforts déployés dans divers domaines et à tous les niveaux : politique, économique, social, diplomatique et autres”. “Des esprits revanchards aveuglés par leur haine et leur rancune envers l’Algérie” Ces efforts ne peuvent être niés que par “des esprits revanchards aveuglés par leur haine et leur rancune envers notre pays”. L’ANP assure en outre à travers El Djeich que “les ennemis de l’Algérie, leurs suppôts, leurs zélés serviteurs, leurs porte-voix médiatiques, les saboteurs qui ont vendu leur âme à vil prix, passés maîtres dans l’art de la trahison, de la félonie et de la servilité”, ne pourront en aucune manière, quoi que puissent tenter, “freiner la marche de l’Algérie ni influer sur la loyauté indéfectible de son peuple à la Patrie.” La bataille d’aujourd’hui est celle de “la conscience par excellence” et le peuple algérien en est “pleinement conscient”. L’ANP se trouve au cœur de cette “responsabilité nationale”, et poursuit avec “une détermination sans faille et une volonté inébranlable” le renforcement de ses facteurs de puissance et de dissuasion afin de faire face aux différentes menaces et de protéger les intérêts supérieurs de la Nation, “à la lumière notamment de la conjoncture qui caractérise notre environnement régional et international ainsi que du caractère interdépendant des sources de menaces”. L’article Menaces contre l’Algérie : El Djeich met en garde contre le triptyque désinformation-sabotage-drogues est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 2027: Afenifere, Ohanaeze, PANDEF, others unite for national cohesion — Igali
items.description: …Reinstates call for 50% derivation to host communities By Henry Umoru ABUJA – The National Chairman of the Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), Ambassador Godknows Igali, has explained how socio-political organisations across Nigeria are collaborating to manage ethnic tensions and promote national unity ahead of the 2027 general elections. Igali said organisations including Afenifere, Ohanaeze Ndigbo Worldwide, the Middle Belt Forum (MBF) and PANDEF had established a common platform, the Southern and Middle Belt Leaders Forum (SMBLF), to promote dialogue and address issues affecting their respective regions. He spoke during a podcast, Conversations with Prof. Jideofor Adibe, where he traced the emergence of the alliance to disagreements between Southern and Northern socio-political leaders over an inflammatory statement allegedly made by an official of the Northern Elders Forum during an election period. According to him, prominent leaders, including the late Chief Edwin Clark, Chief Ayo Adebanjo, Professor George Obiozor and Colonel Dan Suleiman, had approached northern leaders to demand an apology from the individual responsible for the statement. Igali said the failure to secure an apology prompted Southern and Middle Belt leaders to strengthen their cooperation through the regional alliance. He, however, clarified that the development did not end engagements with Northern groups, as the organisations had continued to maintain relationships, consultations and channels of communication. He said the SMBLF initially held meetings every two months and also maintained engagements with the Arewa Consultative Forum and other northern socio-political organisations. “With the Southern and Middle Belt Forum, the Northern Elders Forum and Arewa, we still talk. We attend each other’s activities, we encourage each other, and we have a consultative arrangement,” he said. Igali explained that the arrangement provided an avenue for regional leaders to address inflammatory statements and prevent them from escalating ethnic tensions. “When these inflammatory statements take place, we expect our people to talk to each other so that they don’t overheat,” he said. The PANDEF chairman said the collaboration had also extended to issues of insecurity and the protection of vulnerable communities across the country. He cited instances where youths from the Niger Delta travelled to Benue and Plateau states to express solidarity with communities facing security challenges, describing such gestures as evidence of the need for collective responsibility in addressing insecurity. “Because we are one country, and we have to have peace around the country,” he said. PANDEF renews 50% derivation demand On resource control and revenue allocation, Igali renewed PANDEF’s demand for host communities in resource-producing areas to retain 50 per cent of revenue derived from natural resources within their territories. He argued that communities where natural resources are extracted bear the greatest environmental and social consequences of exploration and production activities and should therefore receive a greater share of the proceeds. “It is important that the community that has the resources keep 50 per cent of the derived resources,” he said. The proposed 50 per cent derivation principle draws on aspects of Nigeria’s pre-independence and First Republic fiscal arrangements, under which regions retained 50 per cent of revenue derived from certain natural resources within their territories before subsequent changes to the revenue allocation system. Igali’s position comes amid continuing calls by regional stakeholders and socio-political organisations for reforms to Nigeria’s revenue allocation framework, equitable development of resource-producing communities and environmental remediation in areas affected by natural resource extraction. The post 2027: Afenifere, Ohanaeze, PANDEF, others unite for national cohesion — Igali appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Simandou Mining Summit 2026 : « La véritable réussite se mesurera aux partenariats conclus et aux projets concrétisés », affirme Namory Camara, Directeur Général du GDB
items.description: En marge de la première édition du Simandou Mining Summit, lancée ce mercredi à Kassa par le Président de la République, Namory Camara, Directeur Général du Guinea Development Board (GDB), revient sur les enjeux de ce rendez-vous économique majeur et sur le rôle de son institution pour transformer l'intérêt des investisseurs en projets concrets. Guinéenews : La première édition du Simandou Mining Summit a été lancée ce mercredi à Kassa par le chef de l'État. Quel bilan faites-vous de ce lancement ? Namory Camara : Ce lancement marque une étape importante pour la Guinée. Au-delà de la mobilisation et de la qualité des échanges, ce sommet montre surtout que notre pays est prêt à engager un dialogue concret avec les investisseurs et les partenaires autour de ses ambitions de développement. Comme l’a souligné le chef de l’État, S.E.M. Mamady Doumbouya, dans son adresse, la Guinée ne vient pas simplement présenter son potentiel : elle met en avant des opportunités sur lesquelles des discussions peuvent s’engager, notamment à travers les rencontres entre les acteurs publics et privés. Bien sûr, nous nous réjouissons de la tenue de cette première édition, mais pour nous, la véritable réussite se mesurera dans la suite, à travers les partenariats qui se construiront et les projets qui pourront se concrétiser. C’est dans cet esprit que nous abordons ce sommet. Guinéenews : Simandou est avant tout un gigantesque projet minier. Comment faire en sorte que ses retombées profitent réellement à l'ensemble de l'économie guinéenne ? Namory Camara : C’est toute l’ambition de la vision Simandou 2040 : faire de ce projet un véritable moteur de transformation de l’économie guinéenne, bien au-delà du seul secteur minier. L’objectif est de créer des opportunités dans des secteurs clés comme l’agriculture, l’industrie, l’énergie et les services, tout en favorisant la participation des entreprises locales. Le GDB joue un rôle essentiel dans cette dynamique en vulgarisant les opportunités d’investissement et en facilitant les partenariats pour créer davantage de valeur et d’emplois en Guinée. Guinéenews : Concrètement, quel rôle le GDB entend-il jouer pour transformer l'intérêt des investisseurs présents à ce sommet en investissements réels en Guinée ? Namory Camara : Attirer l’intérêt d’un investisseur est une première étape, mais le véritable enjeu est de transformer cet intérêt en projets concrets qui se réalisent sur le terrain. C’est là que le GDB entend apporter sa valeur ajoutée : identifier les opportunités, faciliter les échanges avec les institutions et les partenaires, et accompagner la concrétisation des projets. Dans cette dynamique, nous avons organisé, en collaboration avec les ministères et agences gouvernementales, des Deal Rooms durant le sommet, permettant de présenter des projets bancables et concrets aux investisseurs. Notre ambition est de poursuivre ces échanges et de les faire aboutir à des partenariats durables. De plus, notre pays dispose d’un cadre juridique attrayant, avec un Code des investissements très incitatif, ainsi que d’un guichet unique de l’investisseur qui facilite aujourd’hui la création et l’implantation des entreprises grâce à des démarches considérablement raccourcies. Au final, le succès de ce sommet ne se mesurera pas uniquement au nombre de participants, mais surtout aux partenariats conclus, aux projets concrétisés et aux retombées économiques réelles pour la Guinée.

items.title: Burkina: de l’engrais chimique et des boissons frelatées de plus de 13 000 000 FCFA interceptés dans le Nazinon
items.description: Dans le cadre de la poursuite de l'exécution de l’opération WIBGA 3, une équipe du Service Régional de la Police Judiciaire (SRPJ) du Nazinon, en collaboration avec la population, a intercepté, lors d'une mission de patrouille et de surveillance aux environs du carrefour de Nyorida/Manga, deux (02) camions fourgons. En provenance d’un pays voisin, les deux véhicules empruntaient des pistes afin de contourner les postes de contrôle. Le premier véhicule transportait cent vingt (120) sacs d’engrais chimique de 50 kg chacun, et le second véhicule contenait mille (1000) paquets de boissons frelatées. La valeur totale de ces marchandises est estimée à 13.500.000 FCFA. Cette action témoigne encore une fois de la détermination des services de Police en particulier, et des forces de sécurité en général, à lutter contre les circuits frauduleux et à renforcer la sécurité des personnes et des biens. La Police Nationale réitère ses remerciements aux citoyens grâce à qui ce résultat a été atteint. Elle les invite par ailleurs à demeurer toujours vigilants autour d'eux tout en poursuivant la dénonciation des cas suspects aux numéros verts mis à leur disposition que sont les 17, 16 et 1010. La Police Nationale, une force publique au service des citoyens ! items.title: Edo pharmacists, consumer committee clash over drug inspections
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – The Edo State chapter of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) has disagreed with the state Consumer Protection Committee (CPC) over the legality of the committee’s alleged entry into pharmaceutical premises to inspect and confiscate suspected expired, adulterated and counterfeit drugs. The pharmacists accused the committee of exceeding its statutory powers by conducting inspections, seizing pharmaceutical products and imposing fines on operators, insisting that the regulation of pharmacy practice is governed by federal laws. Addressing journalists in Benin City on Thursday on behalf of the Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria (ACPN), an arm of the PSN, the state president, Pharm. Chris Oisakede, said pharmacists had established procedures for handling expired drugs in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC). Oisakede explained that expired medicines were not supposed to be discarded indiscriminately because of the dangers they posed to public health. “An expired drug is dangerous and poisonous, so they are usually gathered and handed over to NAFDAC, which has the protocols for destroying them,” he said. Flanked by other ACPN executives, Oisakede maintained that the CPC lacked the statutory authority to inspect, supervise or regulate pharmacy practice in the country. “For the avoidance of doubt, the Edo State CPC has no jurisdiction or authority, whether directly or indirectly, to enter, inspect, supervise or regulate the practice of pharmacy in Nigeria in any manner whatsoever. “Pharmacy practice in Nigeria, in all its aspects and ramifications, is governed by applicable federal legislation,” he said. He described community pharmacies as important healthcare facilities, noting that pharmacists counsel patients, promote the rational use of medicines, support treatment adherence, identify medicine-related problems and provide medicine safety information. The PSN consequently called on the committee to stop what it described as unauthorised pharmaceutical inspections, raids, harassment, seizures and sealing of premises, as well as the imposition of penalties where it could not establish clear statutory authority. However, reacting to the allegations, the CPC chairman, Osaro Culture Iyamu, defended the committee’s enforcement activities, citing Section 8 of the Counterfeit and Fake Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act as the legal basis for its operations. Iyamu said the provision empowered him to enter premises where there were reasonable grounds to suspect violations of the law, inspect products and examine their packaging, as well as take samples for examination. He added that the law also authorised the seizure of counterfeit, adulterated, banned or fake drugs, confiscation of unwholesome processed food products and sealing of premises connected with suspected offences.
