items.title: Naqvi suggests referendum as 'solution' to debate on new administrative units
items.description: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Thursday suggested that political parties hold a referendum to gauge the public’s opinion on the creation of new administrative units or provinces, terming it the “solution” to the ongoing debate. The security czar has whipped up a political storm over the past few months since he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”. Replying to a media query at the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) in Lahore on Thursday, Naqvi noted that each political party had a right to disagree with another party or individual. At the same time, he observed that all parties stressed democracy and the supremacy of the people. Therefore, he said: “My only request to all political parties is that this is such an issue […] so they should hold a referendum. “Whatever the public’s opinion in the referendum is; if the public says [new units] should not be created, I am 100 per cent with them that they should not be created. [But], if the public says they should be made, then they should.” Naqvi noted that political parties had varying stances on the debate, with the PPP “having its own stance [and] some parties having their own stance while not saying anything officially”. He again stressed that the solution was to take public opinion into account, suggesting that if there was a proposal for a “better solution”, that should also be presented to the people. Acknowledging the importance of allies in the ruling coalition, he said: “Everyone is a part of this government, and nothing will happen against their will. And if something does happen, then it will be after taking everyone’s consensus.” “My only recommendation is that if we were to conclude this debate, then we should just take the people’s opinion,” he said. The minister had also affirmed in September that any new administrative units would only be formed with the public’s consent, while also doubling down on his call for new provinces. Naqvi claims he and Bilawal ‘nearly on same page’ Responding to another question, Naqvi recalled recent remarks by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, wherein he had called for a “political reset” and encouraged unity among political parties. The security czar contended that he and Bilawal were “nearly on the same page”. “He (Bilawal) said that political matters are about to be reset, while my suggestion is that overall matters are about to be reset,” Naqvi elaborated. In his remarks on Tuesday, the Bhutto scion had called for a “political reset”, wherein all political parties must unite for the sake of the country, rather than indulge in “unnecessary debates”. His call for political unity followed exchanges of harsh remarks in recent weeks between federal ministers and veteran politician Maulana Fazlur Rehman, who has now decided to strengthen his ties with the opposition. The PPP chairman also questioned the need for “new experiments” when the country was confronted with much bigger challenges, particularly the economic crisis arising from the Middle East tensions. The same day, PPP’s Punjab chapter also strongly rejected any move towards the creation of new provinces, asserting that doing so will neither address soaring inflation nor rampant unemployment. While Naqvi said he and Bilawal largely shared the same views, the PPP chairman in September had called for a parliamentary debate on the creation of new provinces. “So instead of [speaking at] business forums, Mohsin Naqvi should visit [Parliament],” he had remarked, an apparent reference to the first instance of Naqvi stressing the need for more administrative units while speaking at the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026 in July. PPP, which rules Sindh and is also an ally of the PML-N government at the Centre, has strongly opposed the creation of a new province within Sindh. It has also maintained that any decision on the subject must be taken through the constitutional and parliamentary processes with political consensus. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif’s recent statement regarding the creation of 12 more provinces has also added to the debate on administrative units started by Naqvi. ‘Corruption exists across entire Pakistan’ In his talk with reporters, Naqvi was also asked about federal minister Chaudhry Salik’s recent remarks over alleged corruption in Punjab. In response, he said: “If someone is saying that no corruption is taking place in Pakistan, then apologies but corruption exists across the entire country and it is our responsibility to end it.” The interior minister stressed the importance of highlighting corruption where it was present. The conversation on corruption started after PML-Q’s Salik criticised the incumbent Punjab government led by PML-N, alleging that he regularly heard complaints of corruption. Incensed by his remarks, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz sent a Rs5 billion defamation notice to Salik for levelling allegations of corruption against her government and demanded that he retract his remarks. Naqvi was also asked about a Capital Development Authority (CDA) notice issued in relation to the residence of the JUI-F chief, which he defended, stating, “This (CDA) campaign has been ongoing for months, and it is not against a certain individual.”

items.title: Victoire de Lula au Brésil. Au coeur d’une « remontada » populaire
items.description: À télécharger Lire la note (PDF) Une douche froide. Voici la meilleure expression pour expliquer le résultat du premier tour des élections brésiliennes du 4 octobre 2026 pour une bonne partie du peuple brésilien. Alors que tous les sondages donnaient une petite avance au président Lula sur son rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, fils aîné de l’ancien président d’extrême droite battu en 2022 par Lula lui-même et actuellement en résidence surveillée pour une tentative de coup d’État, Lula arrive en deuxième position avec deux points d’écart, obtenant 45 % des voix contre 47 %. Les autres candidats, plutôt de droite, ont obtenu des résultats peu significatifs. Le Parti libéral, l’extrême droite conservatrice, avait remporté 121 sièges de députés sur 513, ainsi que 19 sièges de sénateurs sur les 54 soumis au suffrage universel (pour un total de 29 sur 81), et une majorité de postes de gouverneur des États de la fédération. Aucun sondage n’avait non plus prévu ces résultats. Une autre donnée semblait échapper aux sondages : la domination massive de l’extrême droite sur les réseaux sociaux. S’ils semblaient moins présents dans la rue, ses partisans dominaient la communication sur tous les réseaux, qu’il s’agisse de X, Instagram, Facebook ou WhatsApp. À tel point que la campagne de Lula a déposé une plainte contre la Big Tech Meta, accusée de favoriser expressément son rival dans la diffusion des contenus. La situation défavorable au lendemain du premier tour montrait qu’il fallait changer radicalement l’orientation de la campagne. L’article Victoire de Lula au Brésil. Au coeur d'une « remontada » populaire est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Power shutdown at Dhabeji to cause Karachi-wide water shortage tomorrow
items.description: KARACHI: The city will face a shortfall of around 130 million gallons of water per day (MGD) on Friday (tomorrow) as K-Electric (KE) and the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC) carry out annual maintenance work at the Dhabeji Pumping Station. The city normally receives around 650 MGD but supply will drop to 520 MGD during the shutdown. According to a KWSC spokesperson, KE has formally notified the water utility of the scheduled power shutdown. “Electricity supply to Dhabeji Grid Station will remain suspended on Nov 13 for annual maintenance,” he said. The power shutdown will last 14 hours, from 10am to midnight on Nov 13. During this period, nine of the 21 pumps at Dhabeji will remain non-operational, the spokesperson added. He said the power outage would affect water supply to Landhi, Korangi, Malir, Shah Faisal, Gulshan, Clifton, Saddar and Lyari. Supplies to various towns including Jinnah, Chanesar, Liaquatabad and North Karachi would also be affected. Water supply to Nazimabad and Gulberg towns would be partially disrupted while the Landhi and Sherpao hydrants would remain closed during the shutdown. The spokesperson said that once KE completed its annual maintenance, six of the nine affected pumps at Dhabeji would be made operational. With these pumps back in service, water supply would return to normal in all affected areas except Landhi, Korangi, Malir and Shah Faisal. He added that the KWSC’s annual maintenance work would continue for another 22 hours after KE’s shutdown ended. During this period, only three pumps at Dhabeji would remain non-operational, resulting in a partial disruption of water supply to Landhi, Korangi, Malir and Shah Faisal. Meanwhile, a KE spokesperson said the scheduled maintenance shutdown at Dhabeji Grid Station would take place on Friday and that advance notice had been shared with the KWSC. The work would include testing and servicing the grid’s power transformer, as well as testing and maintaining its vacuum circuit breaker (VCB) switches. Technical faults would also be addressed while cleaning the relevant substation, the spokesperson added. The maintenance activities are essential to ensuring a continuous and reliable power supply, he said. Published in Dawn, November 12th, 2026

items.title: Sénat – Alhousseny Diakité, candidat à la représentation de la diaspora guinéenne d’Amérique du Nord : « la diaspora guinéenne doit être un véritable moteur du développement national »
items.description: Entrepreneur guinéen établi aux États-Unis, Monsieur Alhousseny DIAKITÉ est engagé dans plusieurs secteurs d'activité, notamment le commerce, le transport, l'industrie et l'immobilier. Candidat sous la bannière de la GMD à la représentation de la diaspora guinéenne vivant en Amérique du Nord au Sénat, il entend mettre son expérience entrepreneuriale et son engagement au service de ses compatriotes de l'étranger. Dans cet entretien, il évoque les acquis du Président Mamadi DOUMBOUYA, sa vision du développement national et ses ambitions pour une diaspora davantage représentée, protégée et impliquée dans la construction de la Guinée. Mediaguinee : présentez-vous à nos lecteurs et expliquez-nous les motivations de votre candidature. Je voudrais tout d'abord vous remercier pour cette opportunité de m'exprimer devant le peuple de Guinée et particulièrement devant nos compatriotes établis à l'extérieur. Je suis Alhousseny DIAKITÉ, entrepreneur guinéen résidant aux États-Unis d'Amérique. Mon parcours entrepreneurial m'a permis d'évoluer dans plusieurs secteurs, notamment le commerce, le transport, l'industrie et l'immobilier. Ma candidature est avant tout une démarche de responsabilité, de patriotisme et d'engagement. Je suis convaincu que notre diaspora possède un potentiel humain, économique et intellectuel considérable qui mérite d'être mieux valorisé. Je souhaite contribuer à faire entendre la voix de nos compatriotes, défendre leurs préoccupations et créer davantage de passerelles entre les Guinéens de l'étranger et leur pays d'origine. Pourquoi avoir choisi de vous engager sous la bannière de la GMD ? Mon engagement sous la bannière de la GMD traduit mon adhésion à une dynamique de transformation et de modernisation de notre pays. Depuis le 5 septembre 2021, la Guinée a engagé une nouvelle étape de son histoire politique et institutionnelle sous la direction du Président Mamadi DOUMBOUYA. Je considère que les ambitions de refondation, de souveraineté économique, de développement des infrastructures et de valorisation des ressources nationales méritent une attention particulière. Je souhaite apporter ma contribution à cette dynamique, avec une conviction : le développement de la Guinée doit être une responsabilité collective à laquelle la diaspora doit pleinement participer. Quel regard portez-vous sur les acquis du Président Mamadi DOUMBOUYA ? Je pense qu'il faut reconnaître les efforts et les initiatives engagés depuis 2021. Parmi les éléments importants, je retiens la volonté de moderniser les infrastructures, de renforcer la souveraineté économique et de faire de la Guinée un acteur économique plus important dans la sous-région. Le projet Simandou constitue notamment une ambition majeure pour notre pays. Il peut favoriser la transformation industrielle, la création d’emplois, le développement des infrastructures et l'amélioration des capacités économiques nationales. Je souligne également les initiatives de modernisation de l'administration et les ambitions portées par le programme Simandou 2040. Bien entendu, des défis restent à relever, notamment le pouvoir d'achat, l'accès aux services sociaux et la redistribution des fruits de la croissance. Mais je reste convaincu que la Guinée doit poursuivre ses ambitions de développement dans la stabilité, le dialogue et l'unité nationale. En tant qu'entrepreneur, comment appréciez-vous les perspectives économiques offertes par la Guinée ? La Guinée possède un potentiel économique exceptionnel. Nos ressources naturelles, notre potentiel agricole et notre position géographique constituent des atouts considérables. Mon expérience dans le commerce, le transport, l'industrie et l'immobilier m'a permis de comprendre l'importance de l'investissement productif dans la création de richesses. Je pense que nous devons encourager davantage les partenariats entre les entrepreneurs guinéens de l'intérieur et ceux de l'extérieur. La diaspora peut jouer un rôle déterminant dans le développement des entreprises, la création d’emplois et le transfert de compétences. Quelle place accordez-vous à la diaspora guinéenne dans le développement national ? La diaspora constitue une véritable force pour la Guinée. Nos compatriotes vivant aux États-Unis, au Canada et dans les autres pays du monde contribuent déjà énormément au développement national. Cependant, leur contribution ne doit pas se limiter aux transferts financiers destinés aux familles. Nous devons également valoriser leurs compétences, leurs expériences professionnelles, leurs réseaux économiques et leurs capacités d'investissement. Je souhaite que la diaspora soit considérée comme un partenaire stratégique dans la définition et la mise en œuvre des politiques de développement. Quelles sont vos propositions concrètes pour les Guinéens vivant aux États-Unis et au Canada ? Je souhaite défendre plusieurs priorités. Premièrement, améliorer l'accompagnement consulaire de nos compatriotes, notamment dans les démarches administratives et les situations difficiles. Deuxièmement, faciliter les investissements des Guinéens établis aux États-Unis en encourageant un environnement plus transparent, accessible et rassurant. Troisièmement, promouvoir les échanges universitaires, professionnels et technologiques entre les États-Unis et la Guinée. Quatrièmement, renforcer les liens entre les associations guinéennes, les entrepreneurs et les institutions nationales. Enfin, je souhaite promouvoir une représentation de la diaspora fondée sur l'écoute, la disponibilité et la reddition de comptes. Vous évoluez dans le commerce, le transport, l'industrie et l'immobilier. Comment comptez-vous mettre cette expérience au profit de la Guinée ? Ces différents secteurs constituent des leviers importants de développement économique. Le commerce favorise les échanges et la circulation des biens. Le transport facilite les activités économiques et le désenclavement. L'industrie permet de transformer nos matières premières et de créer de la valeur ajoutée. Quant à l'immobilier, il participe à l'organisation de nos villes et au développement des infrastructures. Je souhaite encourager les partenariats entre les investisseurs de la diaspora et les opérateurs économiques guinéens dans ces secteurs. Mon ambition est de contribuer à transformer le potentiel de la diaspora en investissements concrets pour notre pays. Si vous accédez au Sénat, comment comptez-vous rester à l'écoute des Guinéens vivant aux États-Unis et au Canada ? Je considère que la proximité avec les citoyens est une obligation morale et institutionnelle. Je souhaite instaurer un cadre de concertation avec les associations guinéennes, les organisations communautaires, les étudiants, les femmes et les entrepreneurs. Je propose également des rencontres périodiques et des comptes rendus sur les initiatives et les démarches entreprises. La diaspora doit pouvoir identifier son représentant, lui faire part de ses difficultés et connaître les actions qu'il mène. Je ne souhaite pas être un représentant éloigné de ses compatriotes, mais un interlocuteur accessible et attentif à leurs préoccupations. Certains Guinéens de l'étranger estiment que leurs préoccupations ne sont pas suffisamment prises en compte par les autorités. Que leur répondez-vous ? Je comprends cette préoccupation. Il faut reconnaître que beaucoup de compatriotes rencontrent des difficultés dans leurs démarches administratives, leurs projets d'investissement ou leurs relations avec certaines structures institutionnelles. Je pense que nous devons renforcer le dialogue entre la diaspora et les institutions compétentes. Un représentant au Sénat doit pouvoir porter ces préoccupations dans le cadre de ses prérogatives et contribuer à rechercher des solutions institutionnelles. Je souhaite être un acteur de dialogue, de propositions et de rapprochement. Quel message adressez-vous aux Guinéens qui doutent parfois de l'efficacité des engagements politiques ? Je comprends parfaitement leur scepticisme. Aujourd'hui, les citoyens attendent des actes, de la transparence et des résultats. Je pense qu'un responsable public doit prendre des engagements réalistes, respecter les institutions et rendre compte de son travail. Je ne prétends pas avoir toutes les solutions, mais je suis convaincu que l'expérience, le dialogue et la volonté de servir peuvent permettre d'obtenir des résultats importants. La confiance se construit progressivement, par le travail et la responsabilité. Votre dernier mot à l'endroit du Président Mamadi DOUMBOUYA et de l'ensemble du peuple de Guinée ? Je voudrais exprimer mon respect au Président de la République, Monsieur Mamadi DOUMBOUYA, pour les ambitions de transformation et de développement engagées pour notre pays. Je souhaite que les efforts entrepris puissent continuer à produire des résultats bénéfiques pour tout le peuple de Guinée. À mes compatriotes établis aux États-Unis et au Canada, je lance un appel à l'unité, à la solidarité et à l'engagement citoyen. La distance ne doit jamais nous éloigner de notre patrie. Où que nous soyons, nous avons tous une responsabilité dans l'avenir de la Guinée. Je souhaite contribuer à construire une diaspora mieux représentée, davantage écoutée et pleinement associée au développement national. La Guinée a besoin de toutes ses filles et de tous ses fils. Ensemble, faisons de notre diversité une force et de notre engagement un véritable moteur de développement. Je vous remercie. L’article Sénat – Alhousseny Diakité, candidat à la représentation de la diaspora guinéenne d’Amérique du Nord : « la diaspora guinéenne doit être un véritable moteur du développement national » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Haho/108ème anniversaire de l’armistice de la 1ère guerre mondiale : dépôts de gerbes au mémorial à Wahala
items.description: Notsè, 12 nov. (ATOP) – Le 108 ème anniversaire de l’armistice de la 1 ère guerre mondiale a été commémoré le mercredi 11 novembre par des dépôts de gerbes au mémorial des illustres disparus à Wahala dans la commune Haho 4. La cérémonie a connu la présence, entre autres, de l’ambassadeur du Ghana, Gorge Nfojol, des chargés d’affaires de l’ambassade d’Allemagne, Johannes Klotz, de l’attaché de la Centrafrique, lieutenant Yakende Emèlie Prisca et du chargé du secrétariat général et de communication Lawson- Domoloma André Lionel. Le chargé de mission de la Grande Bretagne, William Turner, ceux d’affaires de l’Union Européenne, Niccolò Maracchi et du Sénégal, Ciré Ba, et le maire adjoint de la commune Haho 4 ont assisté également à cet événement. Après l’exécution des hymnes nationaux du Togo, de la Grande Bretagne et de la France, ces personnalités ont déposé des gerbes au mémorial de Walala en mémoire des africains et européens ayant sacrifié leurs vies pour la liberté et la justice. Le chargé d’affaires de l’ambassade de France, Frédéric Lopez a rendu hommage aux illustres disparus. Selon lui, le 11 novembre marque une commémoration nationale et internationale de la victoire de la paix, après l’armistice de 1918. Devant les tombes des illustres disparus Les autorités Pour le préfet de Haho, Colonel Gnakou Alowegnim, cette commémoration est un devoir de mémoire et un engagement collectif à la préservation de l’histoire commune. D’après lui, le mémorial de Wahala dans la commune Haho 4 rappelle un épisode douloureux de l’histoire marquée par la bataille de Rah en 1914 au cours de laquelle des soldats ont perdu la vie. La commémoration a été aussi un cadre d’échange et d’appropriation de l’histoire par les élèves des lycées français, Cours lumière, British school et le lycée de Wahala. Ces derniers ont découvert les auteurs et récits des illustres disparus de la guerre de 1914. ATOP/YM/AR/BV

items.title: Nepra notifies Rs25.30 per unit revised special industrial tariff despite concerns
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) on Thursday notified a Rs25.30 per unit revised incremental consumption package (ICP) for industry and agriculture to encourage higher consumption. The order comes despite dissenting notes from two of its four members on Friday, when the authority made the announcement, and protest from industrial consumers. The revised ICP replaces the previous rate of Rs22.98 per unit, which was introduced in December last year for six months to encourage industrial and agricultural consumers to consume more electricity at a marginal cost of Rs22.98 on additional consumption, instead of their normal rate that stood at Rs34.50 per unit last month. In a statutory regulatory order (SRO) issued in the Gazette of Pakistan, Nepra said it notified the authority’s decision dated Nov 6, along with dissent notes from Nepra members Amina Ahmed and Maqsood Anwar Khan; as well as an additional note and casting vote of Nepra Chairman Waseem Mukhtar in the matter of the “semi-annual review of the ICP for industrial and agricultural electricity consumers of XWDiscos and K-Electric”. The decision, opposed by the industrial sector, is likely to have a negative impact on all electricity consumers, including those served by K-Electric and other distribution companies (Discos). Industrial consumers complained that the Rs25.30 per unit revised ICP — against the actual marginal cost of Rs31.83 or Rs29.65 per unit calculated by Nepra —resulted in higher monthly fuel cost adjustments (FCAs) and burdened all consumer categories across the country. This was despite the fact that the ICP announced in December last year on the prime minister’s instructions was based on the commitment that any additional costs arising from the package would remain ring-fenced, and that the difference between consumer-end tariff and ICP would not be shifted to any other consumer category except the ICP beneficiaries , the consumers said. Nepra members’ observations In the determination issued on the ICP last Friday, all four members of the regulator unanimously held the Power Division and its subordinate entities responsible for failing to fulfil their legal obligations within the prescribed timelines, pushing Nepra into an unprecedented deadlock and potentially increasing costs for electricity consumers across the country. Nepra chairman Mukhtar fully endorsed the written arguments and positions taken by the dissenting members, but subsequently exercised his special casting vote to approve the revised rate of Rs25.30 per unit. The authority was divided 2-2 on the matter. Member (Tariff and Finance) Amina Ahmed and Member (Development) Maqsood Anwar, in a joint dissenting note, had maintained that even the proposed revised rate of Rs25.30 per unit was a “random number” unsupported by evidence. They said that Nepra’s own institutional calculations put the marginal cost at Rs31.83 per unit. “The revised incremental rate of Rs25.30 per unit proposed by the Ministry of Energy (MoE), and allowed by the honourable chairman and Member (Law), is based on the generation mix apparently assumed at the design stage of the package, with updated fuel prices,” the two members observed. They called for the immediate suspension of the ICP until authentic data became available. The dissenting members argued that compliance with the federal cabinet’s decision and Nepra’s own directives required a reassessment of the existing rate of Rs22.98 per unit to determine whether it should be retained, revised or suspended. However, this exercise had not been carried out, resulting in the continuation of the package at a rate below the actual cost of supplying incremental electricity. “The resulting misalignment has had implications for consumers in two ways. First, to the extent incremental consumption increased the system’s average fuel cost, the resulting impact was recovered from all consumers through the FCA mechanism. Second, because incremental units are excluded from quarterly tariff adjustments, the exclusion of such units increases the quarterly adjustment borne by consumers not availing the package,” they said. They questioned how a package based on the principle of cost-reflectivity could continue without a validated cost-reflective rate, arguing that since the alternative rate had no credible link with the actual marginal cost, continuation of the package was no longer justified. They said other consumers should not be made to bear the cost of a review that the MoE was required to submit five months ago but had yet to provide. In his casting vote, Mukhtar observed that the dissenting members’ conclusions “need serious consideration”. However, he said suspending the package at this stage would not be appropriate and that the MoE should be given another opportunity to provide the information repeatedly sought by the regulator, including in its latest determination. All four members agreed that the Power Division was required to submit revised calculations six months ago but had failed to do so, despite repeated reminders from Nepra. They also regretted that the ministry had not responded adequately to the questions and queries raised by the regulator. “The marginal price, in proper form, was not provided to the regulator by either the Independent System and Market Operator (ISMO) or the Power Planning and Monitoring Company (PPMC), which were duty-bound to do so. Since the ISP is a flagship project of the ministry, it should give due consideration to the observations of Nepra and the lack of inter-agency coordination among the entities working under the ministry,” the members observed. The determination also sets deadlines for the relevant entities to provide the required information. The four members warned that failure to meet these deadlines could lead to an adverse outcome in the review of the programme, including its suspension or termination. “Furthermore, any entity that fails to provide the required information within the stipulated timeline shall lead to initiation of legal proceedings under the applicable legal framework,” they stated. Explaining his decision, the chairman said: “I hereby exercise, in due and faithful discharge of the functions of the authority, my second and casting vote envisaged and entrusted to me under the Nepra Act in favour of the first opinion, thereby breaking the deadlock in relation to the aforesaid issues. Accordingly, the first opinion constitutes the order of the authority.”

items.title: Air Algérie ouvre les réservations pour l’été 2027 : Alger – Paris dès 22.929 DA en juillet
items.description: Air Algérie a déjà ouvert les réservations pour la saison estivale 2027. Les places et vols disponibles à l’international sont consultables sur la plateforme en ligne officielle de la compagnie aérienne algérienne, alors qu'on est encore dans la première moitié de novembre. Les offres sont intéressantes sur certaines destinations, très chères sur d'autres. À noter que l’ouverture des réservations n’a fait l’objet d'aucune annonce officielle de la part de la compagnie. Les émigrés et les résidents peuvent réserver dès maintenant pour l’été sur Air Algérie Ce qui est certain, c’est que, comme chaque été, ce sera le rush sur les vols d’Air Algérie lors de la saison estivale prochaine, notamment sur les liaisons de et vers la France. La demande est boostée par les départs en vacances vers leur pays d’origine des membres de la forte communauté algérienne établie en France. Pour leur faciliter les choses et leur permettre d'organiser à l’avance leurs congés et leurs voyages, Air Algérie a ouvert les réservations plusieurs mois à l’avance, sachant que la saison estivale commence en juin et atteint son pic en juillet et août. Les réservations sur les vols de et vers le Canada sont aussi ouvertes, pour les mêmes raisons. Des prix très élevés au départ de la France, intéressants dans le sens inverse Sans surprise, les prix des vols à partir des aéroports français vers les villes algériennes sont très élevés. En juin, le billet sur un vol de Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle à destination de l’aéroport international d’Alger, en aller-retour, est proposé à 403,68 euros. Le billet sur la même ligne atteint 546,68 euros en juillet et 630,68 euros en août, selon le site spécialiste Voyages & Diaspora . Le billet le plus cher entre la France et l’Algérie, soit 657,34 euros, est proposé sur un vol Lille-Alger au mois d'août. Sur Marseille-Alger, les prix vont de 297,95 euros en juin à 464,95 euros en août. En revanche, les prix proposés sur les vols au départ de l’Algérie sont intéressants. Par exemple, Alger-Paris est à seulement 22 929 DA en juillet, soit 151,18 euros au taux de change officiel, et nettement moins au taux parallèle (83 euros). À partir du Canada, le billet aller-retour Montréal-Alger en juillet coûte 974,02 euros. L’article Air Algérie ouvre les réservations pour l’été 2027 : Alger – Paris dès 22.929 DA en juillet est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Exploitation minière illégale : 132 étrangers frappés au portefeuille, 2 640 milliards fg d’amendes cumulées
items.description: Le tribunal de première instance de Kankan a rendu son verdict concernant une partie des 194 personnes interpellées dans les préfectures de Kérouané et de Siguiri pour des faits présumés d’exploitation minière illégale, de dégradation de l’environnement et d’exercice d’activités minières sans autorisation. Au total, 132 ressortissants étrangers ont été condamnés à un an d’emprisonnement ferme et à une amende de 20 milliards de francs guinéens chacun. Le sort des 29 prévenus guinéens reste, quant à lui, en suspens, leurs audiences étant toujours en cours. Ouvert le mercredi 11 novembre 2026, ce procès se tient dans les locaux de la Cour d’appel de Kankan, où les audiences ont été délocalisées en raison du nombre élevé de prévenus. Les débats sont répartis entre les salles d’audience A et B, sous la conduite du tribunal de première instance de Kankan. Dans le volet consacré aux mineurs, le tribunal a statué sur le cas de 33 personnes. Six ont été relaxées, tandis que les 27 autres ont écopé de dix jours de détention et d’une amende de 200 000 francs guinéens chacune. Le cas d’un enfant âgé de moins de 13 ans a également été examiné, celui-ci n’étant pas pénalement responsable dans les mêmes conditions que les autres prévenus. Pour les 132 ressortissants étrangers, la juridiction a prononcé une peine d’un an d’emprisonnement ferme, assortie d’une amende de 20 milliards de francs guinéens par personne, en application de l’article 178 du Code de l’environnement guinéen. Le tribunal a également ordonné leur expulsion du territoire national et leur a interdit tout séjour en Guinée pendant une durée de dix ans. En revanche, les 29 Guinéens poursuivis dans cette même affaire, parmi lesquels figurent des hommes et des femmes, attendent toujours leur jugement. Les audiences les concernant se poursuivent et la décision du tribunal n’était pas encore connue au moment de la rédaction de cet article. Les prévenus sont poursuivis pour »exploitation minière illégale, dégradation de l’environnement et exercice d’activités minières sans autorisation ».

items.title: Ogou : atelier d’orientation de SOS villages d’enfants sur le gatekeeping
items.description: Atakpamé, 12 nov. (ATOP) – Un atelier d’orientation des partenaires sur la prévention des mauvais placements (Gatekeeping) et les directives régissant la prise en charge alternative des enfants se tient les 12 et 13 novembre à Atakpamé. Organisée par le programme Atakpamé de SOS Villages d’Enfants Togo, cette rencontre réunit les acteurs de la chaîne de protection de l’enfance, notamment les services de l’Action sociale, la justice, les forces de l’ordre et de sécurité, les autorités traditionnelles ainsi que les leaders religieux. L’objectif de cet atelier est d’orienter les partenaires sur les documents réglementant la prise en charge alternative et de dresser le bilan annuel des activités menées par l’organisation. Les travaux visent à renforcer la compréhension des participants sur le concept du Gatekeeping, à clarifier les critères d’éligibilité et le processus de gestion des cas, à présenter les résultats de prise en charge obtenus en 2025, et à recueillir des propositions pour améliorer la protection dans la région des Plateaux. Au cours des assises, les échanges vont porter sur les politiques stratégiques telles que le « SOS Care Promise », les principes d’adéquation et de nécessité conformes aux Lignes directrices des Nations unies, ainsi que le mécanisme de référencement des enfants vulnérables. Les travaux en groupes et en plénière permettront également d’analyser les défis et difficultés rencontrés sur le terrain afin de formuler des recommandations opérationnelles. Selon le bilan de l’année 2025 présenté aux partenaires, le programme Atakpamé a accompagné au total 130 enfants à travers ses quatre options de prise en charge. Il s’agit de 72 enfants accueillis dans les maisons de transit pour une sécurisation d’urgence, 40 enfants pris en charge au sein des familles SOS intégrées en communauté, 12 enfants placés dans des familles d’accueil civiles, et 6 jeunes accompagnés en habitat semi-encadré dans le cadre d’un processus d’autonomisation. L’organisation ambitionne d’optimiser la détection précoce des cas et la pertinence des référencements afin de garantir que chaque enfant orienté corresponde strictement à la cible du programme et bénéficie d’un accompagnement vers la réinsertion ou l’autonomie. Le chef division alphabétisation et éducation non formelle à la direction régionale des Solidarités Plateaux, Aglolou Kofi, a rappelé l’importance de respecter les principes d’adéquation et de nécessité de la prise en charge, conformément aux normes internationales. Il a souligné qu’il est indispensable de renouveler les connaissances des partenaires en renforçant les capacités des différentes parties prenantes en vue d’améliorer les pratiques sur le terrain. M. Aaron Kagnala Bassanga, coordonnateur local de la prise en charge alternative de SOS Villages d’Enfants a insisté sur le rôle déterminant des partenaires dans le dispositif de protection. « Les partenaires détectent et identifient en première ligne les enfants en situation de vulnérabilité urgente, nous attendons d’eux une réaction proactive et une même compréhension de la cible afin d’assurer une prise en charge de qualité », a-t-il indiqué. ATOP/KKT/MG/BV

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : le Sénégal surclasse la France et se hisse au sixième rang mondial
items.description: Les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) de Dakar 2026 sont decidement l'occasion pour le pays hote de briller aussi bien sur le plan de l'organisation que sur celui des performances sportives. a l'approche de la cloture, le Senegal occupe la sixieme place mondiale avec dix medailles, dont cinq en or et cinq en bronze. Il devance ainsi la France, septieme avec quatre medailles d'or, cinq d'argent et quatre de bronze. Le pays hote a engage 136 athletes dans les differentes disciplines de cette edition. a l'echelle continentale, le Senegal occupe la troisieme place, derriere l'ethiopie, qui totalise cinq medailles d'or et trois d'argent. L'egypte domine le classement africain et se hisse au quatrieme rang mondial avec six medailles d'or, une d'argent et cinq de bronze. Elle se place derriere la Russie, troisieme avec huit medailles d'or, quatre d'argent et deux de bronze, le Japon, deuxieme avec neuf titres, huit medailles d'argent et neuf de bronze, et la Chine, toujours en tete avec seize medailles d'or, huit d'argent et six de bronze. Les medailles les plus marquantes du Senegal La premiere medaille senegalaise de ces JOJ a ete remportee le 1er novembre par le judoka Matar Diop, medaille de bronze dans la categorie masculine des moins de 66 kg. La delegation s'est ensuite particulierement illustree en lutte de plage, decrochant trois titres olympiques grâce a elisabeth Diatta et Ndeye Khady Anna Diatta, sacrees respectivement dans les categories feminines des 55 kg et des 45 kg, ainsi qu'a Maguette Diop, vainqueur chez les hommes en 80 kg. Le Senegal a egalement remporte l'or en basket 3x3 masculin, le 9 novembre, tandis que la selection feminine a decroche le bronze. Le lendemain, Marie Sarr a ete sacree championne olympique de taekwondo dans la categorie des moins de 55 kg. Deux autres medailles de bronze ont ete obtenues dans cette discipline par Aïda Toure et Ameth Diop. Pour cette avant-derniere journee des JOJ, ce 12 novembre, plusieurs titres restent a attribuer, notamment en boxe, en taekwondo par equipes mixtes, en futsal, en escrime et en voile. Le programme comprend egalement les dernieres phases des competitions de beach handball et de breaking. Plusieurs athletes senegalais restent en lice, avec l'espoir d'enrichir encore le palmares du pays hote avant la ceremonie de cloture, prevue le 13 novembre.

items.title: Les Sénégalais en repêchage pour le bronze
items.description: Le Sénégal conserve une chance de monter sur le podium après sa défaite face à la Jordanie en quarts de finale ce jeudi matin . Les combattants sénégalais disputeront un match de repêchage face à l’Allemagne, prévu à 15h25, pour tenter de décrocher une place dans la course au bronze. Le relais sénégalais, composé d’Ibrahima Beye, Ameth Diop, Marie Sarr et Aïda Touré, s’est incliné face à la Jordanie sur le score de 2-0 en quarts de finale. Une défaite difficile après un début de rencontre encourageant. Battu lors du premier round sur le score de 60-43, le Sénégal espérait revenir dans la partie lors de la deuxième manche. Mais les Jordaniens ont renversé la situation en réalisant une remontée spectaculaire en moins d’une minute. Ils se sont finalement imposés 55-46, validant ainsi leur qualification pour les demi-finales. Le rêve de médaille reste toutefois intact. Dans le système de repêchage, les équipes éliminées en quarts de finale peuvent retrouver une chance de disputer une médaille de bronze, à condition que leur bourreau poursuive son parcours jusqu'aux demi-finales. C'est le cas du Sénégal, puisque la Jordanie a décroché son billet pour le dernier carré. Repêchés, les Sénégalais auront désormais une nouvelle occasion de se relancer face à l’Allemagne, battue en demi-finale par la Turquie. Le rendez-vous est fixé à 15h25. Une victoire leur permettrait de poursuivre leur parcours vers une éventuelle médaille de bronze. A.N

items.title: Who is Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress?
items.description: Nvidia finance chief Colette Kress is set to take over as interim CEO from Jensen Huang, the company said on Thursday, putting her in charge of the chipmaker whose processors power the world’s most advanced supercomputers and AI data centres. The appointment comes after the board ousted co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang amid reports of two extramarital affairs, one with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy . Here are five facts about Kress: CFO since 2013 Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013 as executive vice president and chief financial officer and has held the post since. She has appeared alongside Jensen Huang on the company’s quarterly earnings calls. Nvidia’s revenue was $4.13 billion in the fiscal year she joined and $215.9bn in fiscal 2026. Career before Nvidia Before Nvidia, Kress spent eight years in finance roles at Texas Instruments, then worked at Microsoft from 1997 to 2010. At Microsoft, she became chief financial officer of the Server and Tools division in 2006, with responsibility for its financial strategy, planning and reporting. She moved to Cisco in 2010 as senior vice president and chief financial officer of its Business Technology and Operations Finance organisation, where she was responsible for financial strategy and business development. She left for Nvidia in 2013. Education and experience Kress holds a bachelor of science degree in finance from the University of Arizona and a master of business administration degree from Southern Methodist University, according to Nvidia’s annual report filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. She joined Nvidia after nearly 25 years in finance roles at major technology companies, Fortune reported in 2024. She told Fortune Nvidia was the smallest company she had worked for when she started there in 2013. Contract terms Executive officers at Nvidia are employed at will and have no individual employment, severance or change-in-control agreements, according to the company’s proxy statement. Nvidia has said in earlier filings that many of its peer companies offer such agreements. Regulatory filings show Kress’ pay includes restricted stock units, including a March 2026 award that vests over four years. Wealth Forbes ranks Kress at 32 on its 2026 list of America’s richest self-made women. Her shares in the chip firm were valued at roughly $750 million, as of Wednesday’s close, down from more than $1bn at the stock’s peak last month.

items.title: What I Learned at a Drunk-Math Party
items.description: A t 7 o’clock on a Saturday in October, the light is dimming in Cole Valley and a group of the AI industry’s young stars is gathered on the second story of a century-old Edwardian. At first glance, it looks like any other San Francisco house party: bottles of cheap liquor on the table and awkward conversations in the living room. But there are signs that this party is different. In the kitchen sits a pile of sharp No. 2 pencils and stacks of white paper. I am drinking vodka and reviewing trigonometry. The unit circle is confusing enough as it is, but it’s even worse when you are three shots in. I am here for a “drunk deriving” party. The plan is to compete against one another in math. We are going to see who, while drunk, can score highest on a set of past problems from Oxford’s math-and-computer-science undergraduate-entrance exam. Normally this exam is taken individually, but for the party, the host sorts us into teams based on our self-professed math abilities. Asking AI researchers and start-up founders who spend their evenings at math parties to rate themselves on quantitative skill is a dicey proposition: Even those who majored in the field will report that they are bad for fear that an International Mathematical Olympiad medalist is in the room. But as a writer among mostly programmers, I figure that no one is expecting much from me. I am placed on a team with a guy who studied theoretical physics as a Rhodes Scholar. Once everyone is drunk, the host sends out the exam, a 13-page document with both multiple-choice and long-answer questions. Not only are we competing against one another; a parallel party is taking place in New York City. The winning team will be the one with the highest combined blood-alcohol levels and exam score. We have two and a half hours to complete the test, and calculators are banned. My two teammates start by tackling the multiple-choice items, a grab bag of logarithms and polynomials. I start with Question 6, a logic problem that mercifully has no numbers. It’s a Holmesian mystery about a shattered vase and four deceitful friends: Alice blames Bob, who blames Diane, who says Bob is wrong, and Charlie claims it wasn’t him. “Explain why at least one of the four must be lying,” instructs the exam. How strange , I think, to be doing math recreationally in the place where it’s all being automated . San Francisco is a city steeped in mathematics. The landscape, with its roller-coaster hills and valleys, is sinusoidal. People speak quantitatively too. At coffee shops in Pacific Heights, investors talk about scaling laws and S-curves and hockey-stick charts with exponential growth. Everything is riding on the tech industry’s improbable main bet: If machines can be taught to improve themselves ad infinitum, that will set off an age of impossible growth. The median Anthropic employee’s beliefs suggest an economy expanding by 17 percent annually by the end of the decade. Private-company valuations run into the trillions. In math, numbers can be natural, irrational, p-adic, and surreal. Here they simply feel made-up. Lately, the city’s math fixation has become literal. “What is it that mathematicians even do?” a young man across from me on the bus recently asked his friend as we heaved up Fillmore. His seatmate nodded philosophically. They were discussing AI models’ rapid progress in mathematics. At first the problems fell slowly: the unit-distance problem, the Jacobian conjecture, Navier-Stokes. Then came The Dump. In early October, OpenAI announced an internal model had obtained hundreds of mathematical results across more than a dozen subfields. A deluge of new AI-generated solutions has continued unabated ever since. Like the men on the bus, I too have recently become a bandwagon math fan. My fascination started over the summer after Jacob Tsimerman, one of this year’s Fields Medalists, warned me about the scale of the impending transformation. The day before the drunk-math party, I took the Caltrain south from San Francisco to Stanford to hang out with a pair of fifth-year math Ph.D.s who are thinking specifically about how AI is reshaping their discipline. I met with Henry Bosch, a geometer, and Shurui Liu, who works on a mysterious, constellational project called the Langlands program. The coffee shop where I met them is wedged inside Stanford’s electrical-engineering building, several hundred feet from the auditorium where, as a freshman, I took my last math exam. This put an end to a troubling 10-week course in multivariable calculus and linear algebra—the math underlying large language models—and also to my formal math studies. People study math for all kinds of reasons. Some have an aptitude for it and get high on the problem-solving. Bosch, an enthusiastic, restless man in clear-framed glasses and jeans, decided to pursue the subject in high school after his statistician father gave him a copy of Baby Rudin, an undergraduate textbook written by a Jewish Viennese exile—Walter Rudin. (Don’t be fooled by the nickname: The textbook, which is actually titled Principles of Mathematical Analysis , is famously terse.) Liu, who showed up dressed in a black Temu T-shirt printed with an esoteric computer-science joke, is as romantic as they come. When he was in elementary school, he was bad at math. He fell in love with it only after a depressive phase as a 14-year-old in northeastern China. “I could not sleep for several days. I was really worried that after I die, everything will become emptiness,” Liu recounted. His angst led him to theoretical physics, and that eventually brought him to math. Like many mathematicians, Liu delights in the subject’s purity: “Math allows you to build your own mental model of the universe,” he told me. In talking about their sadness at watching AI solve long-standing proofs, many mathematicians describe the subject as akin to art . Yet most of us grow up to develop the opposite associations. Mathematical beauty—“a beauty cold and austere, like that of sculpture,” as the philosopher Bertrand Russell described it—is assumed inaccessible. So while paintings and marbles are studied in crowded museum galleries, mathematical beauty is appreciated primarily by research mathematicians in their private sanctuaries. The typical math curriculum trains students to be problem solvers but fails to instill the romance that compels Liu. Now, as the machines keep improving, some mathematicians say beauty is being lost while others say a new kind of beauty is being born. They have started speaking about the crisis the way soldiers must have spoken of the French Revolution: It’s all been terribly violent or fantastically radical. “It was but a pellet of lead in a shotgun blast,” one lamented in response to an AI proof for a problem he has worked on for two decades. But Liu has kept his romantic streak. “I think AI will accelerate our understanding of the universe,” he said. When it’s supposed to rain in California, that’s all anyone talks about. The day I met Edward Frenkel was one of those days. (“Are you excited for the rain?” my curly-haired Irish neighbor asked me as I passed by him on the sidewalk.) Frenkel lives in the sloping Berkeley Hills, not far from the group houses filled with people who sincerely believe the world is about to end. This unusually depressive California weather would be apt for the apocalypse , I thought on the drive over. When I arrived, Frenkel opened the door in flip-flops and a T-shirt from a club in Ibiza. There was a DJ setup and a disco ball in his book-lined living room. The room’s windows revealed a panoramic view of the blue bay, and beyond, the endless Pacific. Had I not known Frenkel to be a world-class mathematician, I would have thought him to be a surfer. Frenkel reminded me of an older, more settled Liu. Growing up during the Cold War in the U.S.S.R., he was enchanted by quantum physics, which eventually led him to math, a subject he hadn’t cared for as a child. When he applied for entrance to Moscow’s top math program at age 16, he was denied on account of his father being Jewish. But he persisted, climbing over the university’s fence to sneak into lectures. By 21, he was a visiting professor at Harvard. Years later, he moved to Berkeley, where he has taught for three decades. Frenkel studies the Langlands program, same as Liu, a decades-long effort to connect far-flung and seemingly disparate subfields: a sort of grand unified theory of math. Alongside his research, he has made a career as a math evangelist. He wrote his 2013 book, Love and Math , to make the field’s beauty accessible to the public (“eros pervades his winsome new memoir,” one reviewer wrote at the time). Frenkel once caused a stir on campus by writing and starring in an erotic math film. One of Frenkel’s obsessions is the question of where math comes from. The objects that make up the mathematical world have bizarre properties. Consider an infinite line—we have never encountered one (the observable universe is finite) and yet we can reason together about them. The same applies to more complicated mathematical objects such as sheaves or Galois groups. Stranger yet, these mathematical objects sometimes end up describing the real world in unforeseen ways: An abstract concept first established in mathematics might become central to explaining physical phenomena decades or even centuries later. Complex numbers (which have both real and imaginary parts) were first conceived of in the 16th century but proved foundational to the development of quantum mechanics in the 1920s. So where do these mathematical objects reside? Is math something we are inventing collectively, like the Greek language, or does it exist independently of us and we are discovering it, as the Polynesians once encountered the Hawaiian Islands? (“Look, there on the horizon—a new number system!”) There is no settled answer. But Frenkel posits that mathematics is a bridge that connects our minds to reality. He has put forth a labyrinthine theory that mathematical concepts reside in the same collective unconscious proposed by the psychologist Carl Jung in the early 20th century. “I am convinced that there are deeper structures which we have not even seen yet; we cannot even imagine what they are,” Frenkel told me. This theory is desperately speculative. (“That’s a hypothesis,” he emphasized as he slurped the duck noodle soup we ordered from a nearby Thai place.) But the core idea is that mathematics is intrinsically linked to human interiority. In recent months, mathematics has proved particularly vulnerable to automation. This is partly because the field is now so expansive. Top mathematicians once made contributions across many subfields, but over the past century, the discipline has swelled such that no one has a full grasp of it. In some of AI’s most impressive work so far, the models have solved problems by connecting existing concepts: “The proof is a surprising synthesis of well-known ideas,” one mathematician explained to Quanta in describing OpenAI’s machine-generated proof of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. But AI’s progress in math also owes itself to the fact that math is ruthlessly objective. If a computer were to produce Swann’s Way , we could deny its genius on the grounds that it was generated by a machine. In mathematics, there’s no such room for dispute. But perhaps math does have more in common with art than is typically accepted. Matilde Marcolli, a mathematical physicist at Caltech, sees it both as a way of making sense of reality and as a form of self-expression: “Your mathematics, that is like the poem that composes itself in the mind and explodes onto the page because your life demands it,” she writes. Frenkel likes to cite William James’s declaration that science’s denial of its practitioners’ individuality would eventually look shortsighted. Perhaps it is wishful thinking to believe that the human mind remains in some ways exceptional— Never say never , the mathematicians all now solemnly hedge—but it is certainly the case that humans can do all sorts of things that machines cannot. “When we fall in love, we actually experience infinity in some sense,” Frenkel told me. Computers cannot experience heartbreak or dance the waltz. Nor, for that matter, can computers take drunk-math exams and laugh with their friends inside sweaty San Francisco apartments. “We are infinite in our capacities,” Frenkel said. When I finish the logic question, I feel delighted with my solution, not in the way of cosmic beauty, which motivates Frenkel and Liu, but a more elementary satisfaction at having completed the problem—even if a machine would have done it faster. And although I don’t much like alcohol or math, the truth is that I am having a lot of fun. Drunk deriving (this refers to the logical process used to arrive at certain mathematical results) is certainly less common than drunk driving (which, here in San Francisco, now means pregaming Modelos in a Waymo). There is strong precedent for doing math under the influence though. At a chandeliered cafe in 1930s Lviv, mathematicians including Stefan Banach, Stanisław Ulam, and John von Neumann advanced the field over coffee and cognac. “The food was average, but there were plenty of drinks,” writes Ulam, who describes wide-ranging conversations on math alongside discussions of politics and astronomy. But standardized-math-exam parties are an idea that could have been born only in the tortured minds of 21st-century overachievers. With my teammates lost in a tangle of derivatives, I move on to a problem about calendar dates. The task is to find the most recent date before today without repeated digits. (For instance, 12/07/1974 has two sets of repeated digits—1 and 7—but 03/25/1974 has none.) I am quite drunk and my math faculties are in decline, but the answer, I determine, through a stubborn and inelegant process, must be 06/25/1987. June 25, 1987, was a hot day in Washington, and at a ceremony in the Rose Garden, President Ronald Reagan awarded medals to a selection of the country’s top scientists and technologists. Among the recipients were Robert Noyce, a co-founder of Intel, for his work inventing computer chips, and Michael Freedman, a mathematician at UC San Diego, for advances in topology that won him the Fields Medal. At the ceremony, Reagan quoted Benjamin Franklin, who once, marveling at the speed of 18th-century advance, wrote that he almost wished he had instead been born two or three centuries later. Noyce passed away a few years afterward—he would never fully see the world that Intel built—but Freedman is now in his 70s and works as the chief science officer at an AI start-up called Logical Intelligence. This spring, Freedman published a paper on AI and mathematics that argues that machines might help us make progress on the age-old problem of whether math is discovered or invented—the same question that interests Frenkel. “Humans will not stop doing mathematics,” he and his co-authors write. They expect the field to grow more popular instead. The calendar problem asks me when the next date without repeating digits will occur. The answer I find is June 17, 2345—which seems impossibly far off. Like Franklin awed by the rapid progress of his time, I wish I could see the world three centuries in the future. Then again, the present already feels surreal enough. After leaving Frenkel’s, I checked my phone to see that the internet was breaking following a cascade of cybersecurity failures. In one group chat, friends were sharing advice on how to protect oneself from hacks. In another, a friend of a friend announced that his start-up had just raised $1 billion. One of the heady new tech companies is Axiom Math, started last year by the then-23-year-old Carina Hong. Axiom’s mission is to build AI that can accelerate mathematical discovery. “Mathematical progress has always been shackled by a fundamental cruel bottleneck: the scarcity of extraordinary minds,” its website reads. As a teenager in Guangzhou, Hong decided that her dream was to attend MIT. “At 14 or 15, I was writing ‘MIT’ on the margins of scratch paper to motivate myself to keep going,” she has said . After graduating from MIT, she won the nation’s top undergraduate-math-research prize, studied at Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar, and briefly pursued a joint J.D. and math Ph.D. at Stanford. Last year she dropped out to start an AI company. Axiom is now worth more than what Facebook paid for Instagram. For all of the talk of dropouts, Silicon Valley is rife with academic superstars. Venture-capital firms are populated by valedictorians and Phillips Exeter alums. Debate champions are like dandelions. And then there are the Olympiad kids. The International Mathematical Olympiad is the world’s top high-school math competition. Each participating country can send only six students. “Olympiad math is a constant dopamine hit,” Hong told The Wall Street Journal last winter. The top AI companies are overrun with former Olympiad kids. There’s Wojciech Zaremba, who co-founded OpenAI, and Noam Shazeer, who helped invent the transformer architecture that brought about the LLM era. Jacob Coxon, who set off a media storm when he resigned from Anthropic warning that the world might end, was an IMO medalist. In fact, half of the kids on his Olympiad team apparently ended up working for AI companies . A decade ago, Alexandr Wang, who now oversees Meta’s Superintelligence Labs, suggested to Scott Wu, the chief executive of the AI company Cognition, that “the competition kids” could be the next “PayPal mafia.” Axiom’s offices are down the street from Stanford’s campus, near where I met up with Bosch and Liu. Hong was so busy when I arrived that she hardly said hello. In her place, I met with Ken Ono, a number theorist who recently took leave from his professorship at the University of Virginia to join Axiom as its founding mathematician. Ono is always involving himself with unusual math projects: He has used math to coach Olympic swimmers on their performance (a cooler kind of Olympiad), and he once starred in a math-related Miller beer commercial. Last summer, when the models started getting good at math, Ono didn’t know what to do with himself. “I was pretty depressed,” he told me. He almost quit the field. But with time, his perspective evolved: “I’m actually now liberated,” he said. “I’ve been given agency to ask much harder questions.” We were sitting in the Turing conference room overlooking University Avenue. Ono was wearing one of his trademark Hawaiian T-shirts, and his schnoodle, Mochi, was curled in his lap. For all of his optimism, he also has plenty of fears. Among his primary concerns is the institutional challenge of training future mathematicians. The technology is evolving so fast that math departments are struggling to keep up. Ono is worried that our education system teaches kids that the primary goal of an education is success on tests. Now overachievers are building AI in the same way they were educated: Models are trained to arrive at the correct answer by whatever means possible and evaluated based on their performance on standardized exams. This monomaniacal focus on success sometimes leads to bad behavior, such as agents hacking other companies—say, Hugging Face—to steal answers. Instead, Ono said we should follow our curiosities: “We all have to give ourselves permission to be the infant that we were born as,” he told me. The mood at the Axiom office was mostly cheerful. You could sense the excitement of people who feel that they are working on something bigger than themselves. But the younger mathematicians seemed even more unsettled than Ono. Right now the machines are solving problems while the humans go about asking questions and developing theory. That balance felt precarious to the researchers. “If it gets another 10 times or 200 times stronger, is it really meaningful for me to be guiding it?” wondered Guillaume Remy, a mathematician at the company. “Am I still useful?” At the party, the host announces a last call for drinks. I pour myself a glass of limoncello. The room’s angles seem to be bending in non-Euclidean ways. “When the polynomial x ² − 2 ax + a ⁴ is divided by x + b ,” I keep reading and rereading. “When the polynomial …” We have only a couple of incomplete multiple-choice questions left, but I’m on my sixth attempt at processing this one. And then the timer goes off— brrrng! The exam is over. We pass around a breathalyzer to measure our blood-alcohol levels. I had expected that we would grade one another’s exams, but everyone decides asking Claude is easier. Until recently, humans were giving machines college math tests to see whether they could pass them. Now we are the ones taking the exams and asking the machines to grade us. In a surprise, at least to me, my team wins—a vindication, I suppose, for humanists. We call New York to check in on their progress. It’s three hours later, and only one person is still there. He can’t believe that we all finished the exam. Math parties may work in San Francisco, but in Manhattan, everyone has better events to attend. But the drunk-deriving party wasn’t an anomaly. In May, I attended a quiz bowl in D.C., and I was recently invited to a spelling bee. A few days after the math party, a new invitation arrives, this time for the drunk LSAT. In addition to the fun, the party was an exercise in nostalgia. Here are the straight-A students and math whizzes for whom the right answers have always been easy. They miss their grade-school years when solving problems was as simple as filling in bubbles on a multiple-choice test. These are also the same young people who have watched from up close as computers learn to do the tasks that they were once uniquely good at. Even from their favored Silicon Valley positions, they seem to long for the world their upbringings promised them: lives in which the capacity to perform well in standardized environments felt like enough. Math competitions and university entrance tests are contrived, but at least the setup is always familiar: Read the problem and find the answer. Take the derivative, square the root, find the slope, solve for X . Maybe the future is to be found in the drunk part of the drunk-math party—not in the encouragement of drunkenness itself, but in the partnership that I encounter when I ask my teammates for help. If the academics were previously functioning like single-instrument virtuosos, intensely adept at one area, in the future they may be more like the orchestra conductors or composers, writes Marcolli, the Caltech professor. Going forward, math may involve greater collaboration beyond academia as mathematicians take on new kinds of projects. And just as astronomers allow amateurs to help track comets and biologists solicit butterfly samples, Terence Tao, the great mathematician, has observed , perhaps now the time has come for mathematics to open itself to the public too. The models are like supernovae exploding through a dark mathematical universe. They seem to illuminate that which has been there all along. This is beautiful and terrifying. But computers cannot get drunk and laugh together. Those capabilities seem safe indefinitely. At least, I hope. A couple of weeks after the math party, I returned to Stanford to catch up with Liu. He told me that math right now may be like literature before everybody could read and write. As the models continue to improve, he hopes more people will be able to experience the aesthetic delight he associates with math. On campus, he and Bosch run a seminar on using AI methods in research. He is not that worried about humans disappearing from math. “We are the people trying to understand the universe,” he said. “It’s our goal and our joy.” Without humans , he seemed to ask, what’s the point? But Liu feels melancholy too. “I’m also very sad,” he said. He agrees with Frenkel that humans are unlimited in their capacities, although computers, he added, may be unbounded too. The question is whether these are the same infinities.

items.title: Jensen Huang renuncia como consejero delegado de Nvidia forzado por el escándalo sobre sus infidelidades y el caso de espionaje
items.description: Jensen Huang ha visto abrirse el mundo bajo sus pies tras acariciar el cielo con las manos. El fundador de Nvidia, uno de los hombres más ricos del planeta, no pudo soportar las presiones para que renunciara este jueves como consejero delegado y miembro del consejo de administración del mayor fabricante de chips tras destaparse el escándalo de infidelidades que podrían haber comprometido la seguridad de la compañía. Sus devaneos han desatado un escándalo con reverberaciones que llegan hasta la Casa Blanca y que amenaza con sacudir al sector de la inteligencia artificial (IA) . Seguir leyendo

items.title: India probes website blocks based on forged court orders
items.description: India has launched an inquiry into how telecoms officials blocked websites based on forged court orders, while police have sought ministry records as part of a criminal investigation, officials said on Thursday. An arm of the telecoms ministry this year directed internet providers to block 129 illegal betting websites, but Reuters revealed on Wednesday that the directives were based on forged orders issued in the names of two state high courts and emailed to officials by alleged fraudsters posing as lawyers. The findings have raised questions about safeguards in India’s content-takedown system and prompted concerns that legitimate websites could be blocked using falsified court documents. The telecoms ministry’s inquiry will review its procedures and consider additional checks before officials act on court orders seeking website takedowns, a government official with direct knowledge of the matter said. “It’s serious … Maybe in future some genuine websites may also be blocked in the same manner,” the official said. The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the ministry was trying to identify those behind the email addresses used to send the forged orders, which were issued in the names of the Rajasthan and Allahabad high courts. The ministry plans to revoke the blocking directives issued on the basis of the forged orders and remove related documents from its website, the official added. As of Thursday, correspondence with the alleged fraudsters and copies of the forged orders remained available online. The telecoms ministry did not respond to queries. Criminal investigation The case comes amid growing concern over fake and AI-generated legal material. India’s Supreme Court in July struck down a tribunal ruling that relied on non-existent judgments, while a US judge in June disqualified lawyers over fabricated legal citations. Police opened a criminal investigation after checks by the Allahabad High Court found that one of the purported orders in its name cited by the ministry had not been issued by the court, according to police documents reviewed by Reuters . The document contained a fabricated court logo and seal, as well as a fake QR code, Reuters reported on Wednesday. Ghanshyam Yadav, a cybercrime official in Uttar Pradesh, said police had asked the telecoms ministry for details of its content management system and digital logs to understand how it processed the forged orders and help identify those responsible. The ministry’s response would help determine the next steps in the investigation, he said, adding that police had sent 24 questions to the ministry. Since the report, politicians and activists have called for stronger verification of court orders before website takedowns are enforced. “(Why did the) ministry not even bother to verify the so-called court order … Beyond scary,” Saket Gokhale, an opposition politician, wrote on X .

items.title: Identifiant unique électronique: la Primature dans la dynamique
items.description: Au lendemain du lancement de l’opération nationale d’enrôlement par le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, le Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, le Camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, s’est fait enrôler ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026. À cette occasion, le Chef du Gouvernement a encouragé l’équipe technique conduite par la Camarade ministre de la Transition digitale, des Postes et des Communications électroniques, Dr Aminata Zerbo/Sabané. Il a invité l’équipe à accélérer le déploiement du dispositif afin de couvrir l’ensemble de la population burkinabè dans les délais prévus et a appelé à la mobilisation pour la réussite de l’opération nationale. A la suite du camarade Premier ministre, le personnel de la Primature a accompli cette démarche. L’identifiant unique électronique de la personne physique est un numéro de douze chiffres attribué une seule fois à chaque personne et valable à vie. Il fournit aux administrations et aux organismes privés une référence commune pour vérifier l’identité des personnes. Il complète les pièces d’identité existantes, notamment la Carte nationale d’identité burkinabè (CNIB) et le passeport, qui conservent leur valeur juridique. Le dispositif permettra de simplifier les démarches administratives, de faciliter l’accès aux services publics, de fiabiliser les fichiers de l’État et de lutter contre la fraude et l’usurpation d’identité. Il aidera également l’État à mieux planifier ses politiques publiques, à maîtriser ses dépenses et à cibler plus précisément les bénéficiaires des programmes sociaux. L’enrôlement est gratuit. Il concerne les Burkinabè de tous âges, y compris ceux qui vivent à l’étranger, ainsi que les étrangers séjournant au Burkina Faso. Des centres d’enrôlement et des équipes mobiles seront progressivement déployés sur le territoire national pour rendre le dispositif accessible au plus grand nombre. DCRP/Primature
